`adr-coverage`, the unset-command check, the timed-out / flooded pass condition, the limits argument, the `errors` count in bare `kb lint`, the refusal handlers of the doctor and test commands, the `100644/100755` mode filter in the
committed tree, the gate line in the YAML, one rule name in `DOCTOR_RULE_IDS`, the SIGTERM handler, the stderr flood counter and the stream grace.

**Gauntlet.** Three critic rounds, none empty (`GAUNTLET-LOG.md`, `## M13 P25`).

Round 1 (1 blocking, 4 major, 8 minor): any refusal (an invalid config, a corrupt spec document) made every new gate check pass; the limited runner orphaned the command on Ctrl-C and SIGTERM and a
`setsid` grandchild defeated the timeout; `skeleton-deployed` accepted "Production (never dev)", `localhost.` and IPv4-mapped loopback; the clean-clone rules passed stubs; `adr-coverage` counted a rejected ADR.
Round 2 (0 blocking, 7 major): `kb-synced` could not see an ADR or runbook body or a register edit; `adr-coverage` failed a project that follows the briefs (proposed ADRs); a legitimate multi-MB
`package-lock.json` was reported missing; more stubs; a YAML block-scalar test command was refused; `--rule=smoke` ran the whole default suite. Round 3 (1 blocking, 4 major): quadratic regexes on hostile
files were only fixed at one site (an audit of every `^\s*` and lazy `[\s\S]*?` was needed); `echo x && real` was a "no-op"; `forge kb sync` regressed on an unreadable KB file; a command that exited 0 but
left a child holding the pipe was reported timed out; more permissive stub cases; the evidence record was read from the working tree (a FIFO hung it). Each was fixed with a test that fails without it;
round 3's fixes were verified by the scoped suite, typecheck, lint and boundaries, not by a fourth critic.

## Q220 — M13 P15: authoring roles can write — which grants changed and why, one step reassigned, two steps given `outputs`, the separation-of-duties guard, and what the confined grant still lets through

**Context.** `PLAN-M13.md` P15, owner decision 2026-09-20 (`P11-TRIAGE.md` §4 question 1: yes; question 2: yes, handled by P17). After P14 (`Q212`: a step's claim is its `produces` plus the registry paths of its declared `outputs`, `strict` at every autonomy level for a step that declares `outputs`) and P16 (`Q216`: every path a brief names is in the claim), the roles that author documents may hold `tools.write: true`, because the engine reverts everything outside the claim. `reviewer` and `critic` stay read-only, and the engine, not the reviewer, writes the swarm-review report (`Q217`).

**The inventory, recomputed from the real definitions.** `test/output-contract-known-gaps.test.ts` had 28 `no-write-grant` steps when P14 landed; P17 took the two reviewer steps out (26). Every one of the 26 was verified against the real agent, workflow and brief (analyst 4, pm 4, po 3, architect 7, security 2, test-architect 2, ux 1, data-architect 1, em 1, integration-architect 1) and every row of the triage table matched: the step's agent is an authoring role, its outputs are documents its brief tells it to write, and none is a review of someone else's work. After this piece the inventory is **0** (the triage's target said 2, before P17). The pinned total is 0 and `KNOWN_GAPS` is `{}`; a step that declares outputs for an agent that cannot write them, and is not an engine-written swarm-review, fails the first test.

**What changed (agent, old, new, reason).** Only `tools.write` moved (plus the two ceilings); `exec`, `network`, `deploy`, `git_commit` and every other grant are asserted unchanged.

| Agent | `tools.write` | module `ceilings` | own `ceiling.tools.write` | Steps that needed it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| analyst | false -> true | false -> true | none | `intake:propose-level`, `intake:seed-glossary`, `discover:frame-problem`, `adopt:gap-analysis` |
| pm | false -> true | false -> true | none | `discover:define-metrics`, `define-product:write-vision`, `plan-stages:decompose-stages`, `replan:propose-change`, and (reassigned) `define-product:write-prd` |
| po | false -> true | false -> true | none | `plan-stage:write-epics`, `plan-stage:write-stories` |
| ux | false -> true | false -> true | none | `define-product:write-ux-spec` |
| architect | false -> true | false -> true | **false -> true** | `shape-solution:select-architecture`, `select-stack`, `build-stage:freeze-contracts`, `refactor:state-invariants`, `adopt:reverse-derive-specs`, `migrate:plan-migration`, `replan:impact-analysis` |
| data-architect | false -> true | false -> true | none | `shape-solution:model-data` |
| integration-architect | false -> true in **both** copies (`fm-core`, `fm-service`) | false -> true in **both** modules | none | `fm-service/contract-test-cycle:draft-contract` |
| security | false -> true | false -> true | none | `shape-solution:threat-model`, `harden:security-pass` |
| test-architect | false -> true | false -> true | none | `plan-stage:write-test-plan`, `verify-stage:verify-nfrs` |
| em | false -> true | false -> true | none | `retro:run-retro` (the step `Q208` saw live), `plan-stages:review-stages` |
| release | false -> true | false -> true | none | `fm-mobile/store-release:prepare-store-submission` (declared no outputs, below) |

Not changed, on purpose: `reviewer`, `critic` (judging roles: `write: false` in the definition, the module ceiling, the resolved `.forge/agents` copy of a real `forge init`, and no ceiling anywhere was widened, all asserted); `compliance`, `domain-modeler` (both copies), `facilitator`, `finops`, `orchestrator` (no shipped step runs them or declares an output for them: nothing needs a grant, so none is given, and the exact set of agents that still cannot write is pinned). `diagnostician`, `sre`, `platform`, `mobile`, `techwriter` and the implementers already held `write: true`.

**The one reassignment.** `define-product:write-prd` ran as `po` and produces `Capability` and `NFR`; `05` §5.2 gives the PRD and the capabilities to `pm`, `pm` declares both types as outputs, and `po.system.md` reserves scope to the PM. It now runs as `pm` (`define-product.workflow.yaml`). A new test pins it and checks pm declares every output type of the step. **Not done here (P18):** restoring the `pm.write-prd` prompt specialisation (`git show d241002:packages/templates/templates/prompts/pm.define-product.md`, key must equal the brief basename), and aligning pm's `outputs[]` paths to the registry. No other step was reassigned: none of the 26 needed it.

**Two steps given `outputs`.** Both were `write: false` steps with none, so P7 did not check them and the `Q208` finding 4 failure mode (success with no file) was still live.
- `plan-stages:review-stages` (em): `outputs: [{ type: HandoffRecord, subtype: stage-plan-review }]`. The brief's mandatory product is the verdict `HandoffRecord`; the `Risk` entries are written only when the review finds a risk, so they stay in `produces` (`kb/risks.md`) and are not required. `handoffs.md` left `produces` (the declared output's registry path is claimed already). **The subtype is deliberately not `review-stages`** (critic round 1, major): P7 finds a subtype in a produced entry's `step` value or a `subtype:` line of `delivered`, and pm's `decompose-stages` entry names `review-stages` as its NEXT step (`step: decompose-stages → review-stages`), so an `em` session that edited pm's entry and wrote no verdict would have passed; likewise `prepare-store-submission` ends in `-store-submission`. Both new subtypes therefore appear in no step name and are recorded only by a `subtype:` line, the convention P18 is applying to the other five briefs.
- `fm-mobile/store-release:prepare-store-submission` (release): `outputs: [{ type: HandoffRecord, subtype: store-submission-record }]`. No registered artifact type describes a store submission record (`18` §18.7), so the record stays in `produces` and the declared output is the `HandoffRecord` that registers it (`from: release`, `to: human`, `step: prepare-store-submission → submit`, `delivered`: first `subtype: store-submission-record`, second the record's path). Both briefs now name the register `docs/forge/reports/handoffs.md` (the only file P7 checks) and tell the agent to leave every other entry as it is; `review-stage-plan.md`'s verdict is now the second `delivered` string (nothing reads it: `grep` finds no reader). The brief said "and no other file"; it now says "no other document". Alternatives considered: a new artifact type (a registry, schema, template and migration change, out of scope), or leaving the step unchecked (refused: the failure mode stays open). **Limit:** P7 checks the register entry, not that the record document exists (it is claimed through `produces`, which P7 does not verify): a session that writes the entry and no document passes.

**Spec text (quoted).** `05` §5.3 worked example: `write: true                      # architects don't write source code; the engine confines every step to its declared outputs`; `ceiling.tools.write: true`; briefs `select-architecture-style: prompts/architect.select-architecture-style.md` and `change-impact-analysis: prompts/architect.change-impact-analysis.md` replacing `design-system`/`review-change` (F4 of the triage; the §5.6 handoff example's `step: design-system → initialize-repo` is illustrative and was left). `packages/agents/test/content/a2-roster.test.ts` compares the example with the shipped architect: the P3c exclusion of the `prompt.briefs` keys is removed (they now match), and `write`/the ceiling are asserted. `20` §20.1 `write` row, default column: "implementation roles. Authoring roles hold the grant on the agent (it is not per step); a step of theirs that declares `outputs` has a claim of those outputs plus its `produces` (the documents its brief names), enforced `strict` at every autonomy level (`06` §6.7), while a step that declares none takes the autonomy-default claim policy. `reviewer` and `critic` never receive it; the engine writes the review report (`05` §5.7)." This differs from the triage's proposed wording on purpose (critic round 1: the proposal claimed "strict at every level" for every step of an authoring role, which is false for a step that declares no outputs, and "briefs" as the claim, which is `produces`). `05` §5.5 was not touched. `packages/agents/test/fixtures/architect.ts` (the schema tests' copy of the example) and `schema/load.test.ts` follow the amended example.

**Prompts told two roles they were read-only.** `security.system.md` said "You are read-only and you do not patch anything"; it now says it patches nothing and writes only the documents its step declares (anything else is reverted). `release.system.md` said it "can read history and files"; it now adds "and write the record your step declares". `prompts-b-content.test.ts` asserted `security` was `write: false` and its prompt said "read-only": `security` left that list, and a new test checks every authoring role's system prompt never says "read-only" to a role whose grant says write.

**A brief tightened against a role the grants now make dangerous.** `write-stories.md` told `po` that `owner_role` is "an agent role that exists in this project"; the story's `implement-story` steps (agent `{{ownerRole}}`) give that owner write access to source, so it now says an implementation role that writes the story's code, never a document-authoring or judging role. This is text, not enforcement (`assertPlannable` and the DoR rule refuse only `sdet`/`reviewer`); see the open items.

**The separation-of-duties guard (permanent tests).** `test/authoring-roles-write.test.ts` (definition level, reads the YAML, the module ceilings and a real `forge init` project): every authoring role holds the grant in the `fm-core` definition, the `fm-service` copy, the resolved init agent, and its ceiling permits it; `reviewer`/`critic` are `write: false` in the definition, module ceiling, own ceiling and the init copy and their ceilings equal their grants (no headroom); the **exact set** of agents that still cannot write is pinned; every module agent's grant lies inside its module ceiling (write, deploy, network, exec) and `ceiling.write` equals the grant for every agent; `resolveStepToolGrant` passes for each authoring role and for the shadowing `fm-service` copy, refuses `network: full`, `deploy: true` and an out-of-list `exec` overlay for each, refuses a reviewer/critic write overlay, and refuses the exact pre-fix state (a grant of write over a ceiling of `write: false`); `isEscalationRefused` still refuses an escalation to `write: true` for all four protected roles. `test/authoring-roles-run.test.ts` (end to end, 66 tests): **all eleven roles**, thirteen real shipped steps (analyst `adopt:gap-analysis`, pm `replan:propose-change` and the reassigned `define-product:write-prd` (Capability + NFR), po `plan-stage:write-epics`, ux `define-product:write-ux-spec`, architect `replan:impact-analysis`, data-architect `shape-solution:model-data`, integration-architect fm-service `contract-test-cycle:draft-contract`, security `shape-solution:threat-model`, test-architect `plan-stage:write-test-plan`, em `retro:run-retro` and `plan-stages:review-stages`, release fm-mobile `store-release:prepare-store-submission`), taken from a real `forge init` project's `.forge/workflows` and the two module workflows, run alone through the real `runWorkflow` with a strict fake whose scripted session writes only if `request.tools.write` is true. Per step: the output is written, the step succeeds, P7 is satisfied, nothing is reverted and the output is in the step's own lane; a session that ALSO writes source code, a Waiver (`reports/waivers.md`) and its own `.forge/agents/<role>.yaml` has all three reverted (the agent file byte-equal to the original), the output kept, and one `PolicyViolation` naming exactly those three paths (the test does not assert the step succeeds: whether `strict` fails the step is P31); a session that writes only a stray fails `RUN-083`; a negative control, the same role with `write: false`, gets no write and fails `RUN-084`. For `retro:run-retro`: `supervised`, `autonomous` and `guided` + adopted. Three register cases: an `em` session that only edits the entry pm left in the register (its subtype is `stage-plan`), a release session whose entry names the step but carries no `subtype:` line, and a re-run whose register already holds a `stage-plan-review` entry and adds nothing, each fail `RUN-083` (a mutation back to subtype `review-stages` makes the first pass wrongly, so it fails the test). **Not shown, and not true today:** that another role's entry cannot satisfy the output: P7 does not compare an entry's `from` with the running agent, so a session that adds a `subtype:` line to someone else's entry passes (open item below).
`test/authoring-roles-write.test.ts` also asserts that every shipped agent step of the eleven roles, `onComplete` and `onFailure` hooks included, declares `outputs` (a floor of 25 steps guards against an empty enumeration), because only a step that declares outputs is forced `strict`. Mutation evidence: flipping `em` to `write: false` fails 27 cases across the three files (the definition, ceiling, init copy, both em end-to-end steps, the inventory); flipping `reviewer` to `write: true` fails the reviewer, no-headroom, pinned-set, protected-role and swarm-review tests.

**What could not be stated as a clean invariant, and the narrower true ones.** (The pairs are pinned as two lists: the three that already held at HEAD before this piece, and the two P15 created.) The brief asked for "no agent declares `write: true` together with `gates.may_approve` for the gate that judges its own outputs". That is **false of the shipped roster and was before P15**: `platform` (`G-Foundation`) and `sre` (`G-Deliver`, `G-Operate`) have shipped as writers that may approve the gate they produce evidence for since M6, and P15's grants make `pm` (`G-Product`) and `po` (`G-Ready`) the same (`05` §5.2 says `pm`/`po` cannot approve *engineering* gates, which implies they can approve product ones). The brief also said "a role in `REVIEW_OR_CRITIC_ROLES` stays read-only": that set is `reviewer`, `critic`, `diagnostician`, `test-architect`; `diagnostician` shipped `write: true` and the owner approved question 1 with `test-architect` named ("includes test-architect, a protected role", `P11-TRIAGE.md` §4), so the guard pins the two protected roles that write by name and asserts `reviewer` and `critic` never do. Pinned instead: (1) the (writer, may-approve, evidence-for) triples are exactly `platform:G-Foundation`, `pm:G-Product`, `po:G-Ready`, `sre:G-Deliver`, `sre:G-Operate`, so a new one is a deliberate edit; (2) no judging role (`reviewer`, `critic`, `diagnostician`, `test-architect`) may approve any gate; (3) the only roles that may approve anything are `pm`, `po`, `platform`, `sre`; (4) `architect` and `integration-architect` approve nothing. `gates.may_approve` is read by no run-time code (a gate is approved by a person, `forge gate approve`), so these triples are a declared authority, not an enforced one. **Owner question, not decided here:** should `pm`/`po` keep `may_approve` for the product gates now that they write those gates' evidence? Removing it edits an immutable §5.9 field and the `05` §5.2 roster reading, so it was not done.

**The residual, stated honestly (`P11-TRIAGE.md` §3-§4, `Q212`).**
- The claim is a **type glob, not an artifact id**: `po` may rewrite every `STORY-*.md` and `EPIC-*.md`, `em` every `SESSION-*.md`, `pm` every `CAP-*.md` (and it edits them in `decompose-stages` and `write-epics` by design), every HandoffRecord step can edit earlier entries in the shared `handoffs.md`, and `security` (`harden:security-pass`, `Defect`) can rewrite any `DEF-*.md`; `validate-rules.ts` treats any status other than the literal `open` as closed, so it could flip a Sev1 defect closed inside its claim. `test-architect`'s claim is the `handoffs.md` register plus `specs/test-plan.md`, `kb/engineering/testing.md`, `kb/open-questions.md`. `integration-architect` and `architect` (`freeze-contracts`) hold `specs/interfaces/*` while `spec interfaces --check-frozen` is unimplemented (P26): a frozen contract can be rewritten and nothing checks it.
- Enforcement is **after the fact** (a revert and a `PolicyViolation`), not a tool boundary: the platform grant is the bare `Edit`/`Write` pair (`mapToolGrantToAllowedTools`), not `Edit(<glob>)`. FORGE does not itself confine a session to its lane worktree; that is Claude Code's own working-directory behaviour, not verified here.
- Enforcement runs **only when the adapter reports changed files** (`Q209`, `Q212`): the roles given `write` here have `exec` of `ls*`/`rg*`/`cat*` (and `git log*`/`git diff*`), none can `git commit`, so the "agent commits its own work" skip does not apply to them; a rerolled lane whose new session changes nothing still skips it.
- `strict` reverts and traces but does not fail the step (`Q212`, owner call in P31).
- No cheap mitigation was in scope: per-artifact-id claims and a path-scoped platform grant are the triage's M14 hardening; a check that a `Defect`'s `status` did not move, or that a frozen contract's front matter is unchanged, belongs with P26. Listed for the orchestrator below.

**Existing tests changed (hard-coded old grants, not weakened).** `test/output-contract-known-gaps.test.ts` (inventory 26 -> 0, `OWNERSHIP_ONLY_STEPS` 9 -> 32: the recomputed definition-level class now includes the 21 steps their roles' narrower `file_ownership` never covered, plus the two steps that gained `outputs`; each is asserted inside its own claim; the `retro:run-retro` test now asserts em writes and its output is checked; new assertions for `write-prd` and the two new outputs); `test/agent-prompts-all-workflows.test.ts` (P6 asserted that some dispatched agent step has `write: false`; none does any more, so the read-only side is now proven by the interaction-mode participants each carrying a grant with neither `write` nor `exec`, and the ordinary agents are told apart by their exec allowlists); `packages/extensions/test/module/fm-service.test.ts` (ceiling `write: true`); `test/fm-mobile-workflow.test.ts` (the fake session also writes the handoff entry); `a2-roster.test.ts` and `prompts-b-content.test.ts` (above).

**Three critic rounds** (`GAUNTLET-LOG.md`, `## M13 P15`): round 1 one blocking (the `{{ownerRole}}` hole, disclosed, the brief and the `Story.md` template placeholder tightened) and six major; round 2 no blocking and two major (the confinement wording, the subtype test's overstated title); round 3 (after the spend-limit cutoff, re-dispatched) no blocking and three major: the missing Q entry (this one), the two new briefs' `subtype:` sentence being pinned by nothing (now pinned), and the `20` §20.1 sentence still implying a per-step grant (reworded above; the deferral of an engine-side rule is recorded below).

**Found, not fixed (the orchestrator turns these into pieces).**
- **`Story.owner_role` is not restricted to implementation roles (critic round 1, blocking, real).** `implement-story:{plan,green,refactor,document}` run as `{{ownerRole}}`; `assertPlannable` (`cli/src/commands/run/expression-context.ts`, P21's file, not touched) refuses only `sdet`/`reviewer`, and `Story.owner_role` is any non-empty string. A story owned by `security`, `pm` or `release` now runs with `write: true`; `refactor` and `document` have no claim at all (`brief-write-paths-in-claim`'s `KNOWN_EMPTY_CLAIM`), so under `guided` (`warn`) everything they write is kept and under the strict levels everything is reverted while the step succeeds. Before P15 such an owner was silently a no-op. Same shape as for any implementer under `warn`, but the set of roles that can now be an owner is wider. Recommended piece: refuse a non-implementation `owner_role` in the DoR rule and `assertPlannable` (the set is the roles that hold `write` and are not in the authoring list), and give `refactor`/`document` a claim (`{{run.filesExpected}}`); the write-stories brief text is the only mitigation done.
- **P7 does not check an entry's `from` against the running agent**, so a `subtype:` line added to someone else's entry satisfies a `HandoffRecord` output (round 2, major, real, engine-side).
- **A step that declares no `outputs` is not confined, and the grant does not know it.** `assemble.ts` grants `write` from the agent definition alone (only a tainted step loses it) and `resolveStepClaim` forces `strict` only when `outputs` are declared, so an authoring role on a user-authored step with no outputs, on a stale materialised project copy of a workflow whose step gained `outputs` in this piece (`plan-stages`, `store-release`), or as `{{ownerRole}}`, writes with the autonomy-default policy (`warn` at `guided` keeps out-of-claim files). The shipped workflows have none (a test walks them, `onComplete`/`onFailure` included; a `{{ownerRole}}` step is invisible to it). Recommended (fail closed): an agent step whose claim is empty (no `outputs`, no `produces`) runs with `write: false`, or workflow validation refuses an authoring-role step without `outputs`. The spec 20 §20.1 and the architect/§5.3 comments say only steps that declare outputs are confined, for that reason.
- **A writing role can rewrite or delete other roles' entries in a shared register** (`handoffs.md`, `risks.md`, `open-questions.md`, `assumptions.md`) as long as it adds or changes one of its own; P7 compares neither surviving entries nor `from:` provenance. The briefs tell each agent to leave the others alone; nothing checks. Recommended: a P7 register rule (surviving base entries byte-equal, or only the entries this step's role authored changed).
- **`kb_write` and `file_ownership` are enforced nowhere, and `05` §5.2 roster rule 3 ("only the owning agent's writes are auto-applied") is not implemented:** 32 write steps write outside their agent's `file_ownership` (the ratchet in the known-gaps test), several outside `kb_write` (`security` writes `kb/architecture/`, `analyst` `kb/glossary.md`), every one of those agents declares `exclusive: true` so `forge agent validate`'s overlap check validates a declaration the shipped workflows violate, and 18 write steps declare outputs their agent's own `outputs[]` lacks (P18). Decide whether the claim or ownership is authoritative and amend `05` §5.2 accordingly, or make ownership the claim's ceiling (path-scoped grants, M14).
- Spec `06` §6.7 still says `strict` fails the step; the code reverts and traces (`Q212`, P31). Spec `15` §15.3.2 and `REVIEW_OR_CRITIC_ROLES` (`reviewer`, `critic`, `diagnostician`, `test-architect`) refuse a `write: true` ESCALATION for all four; the shipped base grants of `diagnostician` and now `test-architect` are not escalations, and `resolveStepToolGrant` has no independent floor for the role tag (a reviewer definition with `write: true` and a matching ceiling would resolve): the guard is the shipped-file tests.
- Existing projects keep materialised `.forge/agents/*.yaml` with `write: false` (a generated copy): their first run of one of these steps fails `RUN-084` until the file is regenerated (`forge upgrade`); no drift notice was added.
- `fixtures/greenfield-service/.forge/{agents,workflows}` and its manifest are frozen snapshots (`write: false`, `write-prd` on `po`); not loaded as agents (P18 regenerates). The new prompt test scans only `*.system.md` for "read-only", not briefs (a brief's "the repository, read-only" is about the tree, not the grant).
- `pm` runs `write-prd` with no `pm.write-prd` brief specialisation and its `outputs[]` paths disagree with the registry (P18).
- Adversarial only, pre-existing: claim enforcement lists changes with `--exclude-standard`, so a write to a gitignored path is invisible to it; `exec` patterns such as `git log*` and `rg*` admit `--output=`/`--pre` (writes and execution outside the write grant). `write: false` never was a barrier against those; P28's confinement work is where they belong.
- `test/forge-debug-real-project.test.ts` fails (`needs-more-evidence`, expected `escalated`) with or without this piece's module edits (confirmed by reverting them): another piece's in-flight change.
- `may_approve` is inert and now names writers for their own evidence (owner question above).

**Verification scope (owner-approved cost cut; no full unscoped suite).** Root `test/{authoring-roles-write,authoring-roles-run,output-contract-known-gaps,agent-prompts-all-workflows,workflows,build-stage-compiles,workspace-floor,fm-core-module,fm-service-workflow,fm-mobile-workflow,live-smoke,determinism,brief-write-paths-in-claim,strict-opt-outs,templates,gates,command-steps,frameworks,lint-rules,run-inputs-compile}.test.ts`; all of `packages/agents`, `packages/extensions/test/module`, `packages/engine/test/{dispatch,run,gates,interaction}`, `packages/cli/test/{init,e2e,commands/{agent,overlay,module,gate-validate,run,loop,workflow,doctor}}`, `packages/sessions`, `packages/kb/test/adopt`; `pnpm typecheck` (root `tsc` clean; only another piece's `engine/test/plan/command-quoting.test.ts` fails in turbo), `pnpm run boundaries`, `eslint`/`prettier` on every file owned. Failures seen and not mine: `forge-debug-real-project` (above), `workspace-floor` (engine typecheck of the same in-flight file), and the known load flakes (`resume.test.ts`, `status.test.ts`: pass alone).

## Q222 — M13 P28: model-proposed commands are confined, a tainted step's grant is restricted, `forge debug`'s FIX diff is scanned, and substituted values are shell data — the inventory, the decisions, and what is left open

**Context:** `PLAN-M13.md` P28 (security); Q215 findings 3 and 4 (`forge debug`'s REPRODUCE/PROVE commands ran through `runShellCommand` with `shell: true`, the whole environment, no grant; "nothing restricts a tainted FIX"; no claim or output scan on the diff `forge debug` commits); Q203 D8 ("no consumer restricts a tainted agent step's grant; the decider keeps its write grant"); Q212 (P14 claim enforcement). Specs: `20` §20.1 (exec allowlist matched against the parsed command, shell metacharacters deny, anchored patterns, the hard denylist "overrides every allowlist and every autonomy level", `network: none` by default), §20.2 (path containment, deny list `.git/`, `.forge/state/`, `.env*`, `node_modules/`, secret-file patterns; claim enforcement), §20.4 (secrets exist only in the environment of the process that needs them; pre-commit secret scan), §20.5 (points 3-5: taint loses privileged actions, "capability restriction is the control", output scanning), §20.10 S2/S3/S4/S6; `15` §15.5.4; `05` §5.4 point 6; `13` §13.2 F-DEBUG-1 steps 2, 7, 8; `06` §6.7.

### 1. The inventory (verified by reading each call site, not derived from the P27 list; pinned by `test/shell-sinks-inventory.test.ts`)

Every production file that starts a shell (`execa(..., { shell: true })`, `runShellCommand(...)`, `child_process`), where its command text comes from, what stands between the text and the shell today, and the status after this piece:

| Sink | Source of the text | Checks after P28 | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `engine/dispatch/confined-command.ts` (via `createRcaShell`, called by `cli/commands/loop/debug.ts`) | a shell command a **model** proposed: `forge debug` REPRODUCE, PROVE | see §2: denylist, operator veto, expansion refusal, the agent's exec patterns, network policy, lane containment, dangerous arguments; scrubbed env, closed stdin, lane cwd, timeout, output cap | **confined** (was: unchecked, the only model-to-shell path found) |
| `engine/dispatch/steps.ts` (2) | `kind: command` step `run:` (workflow YAML by the project or a module) with run inputs, story/epic fields, fanout items, stage vars substituted | every substituted value is shell-quoted at the interpolation point (§5); P21 also refuses shell-unsafe `--input`/`--stage`/`--epic`/`--story` at parse time (RUN-088); the `run:` text is the workflow author's, not grant-confined; env is the parent's plus `commandEnv` | **quoted** (was: unquoted, `stageId`, `defectId`, `{{item.id}}` were code) |
| `engine/dispatch/facades.ts` (2), `cli/commands/run/gate-commands.ts` (2) | gate `check.run` (gate YAML in `.forge/checks`, module/overlay authored), merge pre/post checks | no interpolation of run inputs or model text; author-trusted | trusted |
| `cli/commands/loop/test/{run,layer}.ts`, `reporter.ts` | `execution.testCommands.*` from `.forge/config.yaml`; `reporter.ts` adds a file path and a test name from a previous report | user-authored config; the two added values pass `shellQuote` | trusted / quoted |
| `vcs/claims.ts` | `applySharedPathStrategy` `regenerate` command (workflow/config) | author-trusted, no interpolation | trusted |
| `engine/adopt/verification.ts` | `forge adopt` phase 5: build and test commands **derived from the brownfield repository** (package scripts, Makefile, Dockerfile CMD): text a third party wrote | timeout, throwaway clone; whole parent environment; no grant, no denylist | **open, disclosed** (§8) |
| `cli/commands/kb.ts` | `forge kb verify`: the command stored in a KB entry (written by agents and `forge adopt`) | timeout, truncated output; runs in the LIVE tree with the whole environment | **open, disclosed** (§8) |
| `engine/dispatch/shell.ts` | the shared runner | none of its own | trusted |

Not shells but worth naming: adapters start `claude`/a configured binary with an argv and a `{{...}}`-templated argument list (no shell); `@forge/vcs` and the doctor/adopt/extension code run `git`/`npm` with argv arrays (no shell). Text a model writes can still become code **indirectly**: a file it writes that a later `command` step or `forge test run` executes (tests, scripts, `package.json` scripts). No shell check can see that; §8. A model's own Bash tool inside an adapter session is governed by the adapter's grant mapping (`isExecAllowed`, `07` §7.2), not by this piece.

### 2. Confining what a model proposes (`engine/dispatch/confined-command.ts`, `engine/rca/shell.ts`)

`RcaLoopDeps.runShell` is now `(command, cwd, origin: 'proposed' | 'engine') => RcaShellResult`. The loop passes `proposed` for the reproduction command (REPRODUCE, and again in PROVE) and `engine` for `forge test run` and the revert-check script (which wraps a command already vetted moments earlier). `createRcaShell` vets `proposed` commands and runs both origins confined.

**Vet order** (`vetProposedCommand`; first refusal wins; every refusal has a reason category and one line naming the word that did it): (1) empty, over 2000 chars, NUL: `malformed`; (2) `isHardDenylisted` (S2): `denylisted`; (3) `SHELL_OPERATOR_PATTERN` over the WHOLE raw string, quoted or not, and for exact patterns too: `shell-operator` (so a model never gets a chained command even where a pattern was written out in full); (4) a quote-aware word split that refuses what the shell expands before the program starts: `$` outside single quotes, `~` at the start of a word, backslashes, unquoted `(`/`)`, an unquoted `#` word (a comment: it would also swallow the revert-check's closing paren), brace lists, unterminated quotes: `expansion`/`shell-operator`/`malformed`; (5) the agent's exec patterns through `isExecAllowed`, AND the first word must be the program the matching pattern names (`cat*` also matches `catdoc`, `lsof`), AND a leading `VAR=x` word is refused (`ls=1 node -e ...` matches `ls*` as a string; the shell runs `node`): `not-in-grant`/`shell-operator`; (6) network: the program (`curl wget ssh scp nc rsync ...`), git subcommands that reach a remote (`push fetch pull clone ls-remote remote submodule ...`), package managers (`npm pnpm yarn pip cargo`) unless the FIRST argument is a test verb (`test`, `run`), because the verb cannot be found behind flags that take a value (`pnpm --filter x install`, a bare `yarn`, `dlx`, `exec`), all unless the grant's `network` is `full`; every URL/`user@host:` word checked with `isHostAllowed`: `network`; (7) **git is an allowlist**: only read-only subcommands (`log diff show status rev-parse rev-list ls-files ls-tree cat-file blame grep shortlog describe name-rev merge-base show-ref for-each-ref diff-tree reflog ...`) whatever a `git *` grant says (git has too many subcommands that reach a remote or run a program for a blocklist: `archive --remote`, `send-pack`, `for-each-repo`, `bisect run`, `p4`); options before the subcommand other than `-C <dir>`, `--no-pager` and a few switches are refused (`-c`, `--config-env`, `--exec-path`, `--attr-source`: fail closed on an option that takes a value and would shift the subcommand); git accepts any unambiguous PREFIX of a long option, so an argument is refused when what it names is the start of `--open-files-in-pager`, `--ext-diff`, `--output`, `--upload-pack`, `--receive-pack`, `--exec`, `--exec-path`, `--config-env` or `--remote` (`--open=sh` is `--open-files-in-pager=sh`), and `-O<x>`; other programs: `rg --pre`, `rg --hostname-bin`, `tree -o`: `dangerous-argument`/`network`; (8) path containment for every word, every `=` part, every `:` part (`git show HEAD:.env`), and whatever follows a slash in a flag word (`-n5/etc/x`); an unquoted glob (`*`, `?`, `[`) is EXPANDED here, one segment at a time, reading only the depth the pattern reaches, and every match is checked as if written out (a tracked file named `--open-files-in-pager=sh` would turn `*` into an option, `cat .env*` is `cat .env`, `link/*` passes through a symlink; a match starting `-`, leaving the lane or naming a secret is refused; more than 20 000 entries needed: refused); outside the lane, `..` escaping, `.*`-style globs that can match `..`, a symlink whose target is outside (`realpath`): `path-escape`; secret files and internals (`.env*`, `.git`, `.forge/state`, `.ssh`, `.aws`, `*.pem`, `id_rsa*`, `.npmrc`, ...): `secret-path`.

**Execution** (`runConfinedCommand`): `env` = `scrubbedEnvironment(parentEnv)` with `extendEnv: false`. `CONFINED_ENV_ALLOWLIST` is an allowlist, defined once: `PATH HOME USER LOGNAME SHELL LANG LANGUAGE TERM TZ TMPDIR TEMP TMP CI NO_COLOR SYSTEMROOT` and the `LC_*` family, plus fixed `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 GIT_PAGER=cat PAGER=cat`; for a `proposed` command also `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1` (no alias, credential helper or `core.hooksPath` from the user's config through `git *`). A test asserts the allowlist names nothing credential-shaped. `stdin: 'ignore'`; cwd = the lane; `detached` process group killed on timeout, output overflow and process exit (a grandchild cannot hold the pipes open); defaults `PROPOSED_COMMAND_LIMITS` = 120 s / 1 MB, `ENGINE_COMMAND_LIMITS` = 20 min / 8 MB. `parentEnv` is required (R10: `bin.ts` reads `process.env` once; `DebugDeps.env`, supplied by `buildLoopDepsForProject`).

**Result and evidence.** A refusal is a result, not an exception: exit `126`, empty output, `refusal: {code: 'RUN-095', reason, detail, message}`, nothing executed. The loop records it in `RcaLoopResult`'s `refusedCommands` (on `needs-more-evidence` and on the `escalated` evidence bundle; the key is present only when there is one), marks the attempt `<command> [refused (<reason>)]` in the fenced `prior-attempts` data the next REPRODUCE sees, and writes the instrumentation plan line "was not run to a verdict — propose a command the agent's tool grant allows, or widen `tools.exec` deliberately". **A refusal, a timeout and an output overflow are never a reproduction** (their non-zero exit codes used to count as one): REPRODUCE skips them, PROVE treats a refused or killed reproduction, or a killed `forge test run`, as not proved. `forge debug` also emits a `PolicyViolation` event (`kind: proposed-command-refused`, code, reason, capped command) per refusal. New codes `RUN-095` (a proposed command refused) and `RUN-096` (a FIX diff refused), in `codes.ts`; RUN-088..RUN-092 are P21's, RUN-093/094 are left unused for the concurrent pieces.

### 3. Decisions for the owner

**D1. The commands FORGE runs for a model are held to the agent's resolved, UNTAINTED grant.** The reproduction command is model output, and the REPRODUCE phase carries fenced defect text, so a strict reading of `20` §20.5 ("tainted: no exec") would refuse every proposed command and `forge debug` could never leave REPRODUCE (`13` §13.2 step 2 makes reproduction a hard gate). The grant used is what `preflightDebug` resolves for the FIX phase before anything is tainted: the diagnostician's own `exec` patterns and `network`, i.e. what the agent could run itself. Alternative: refuse all proposed commands (debug becomes a documentation tool). Recommended as built.

**D2. The shipped diagnostician's exec patterns are too narrow for a useful RCA loop, and this piece does not widen them.** `git *`, `ls*`, `rg*`, `cat*`, `tree*` allow no test runner, no `node`, no `pnpm`, so the only reproductions that can run are read-only (`cat missing.txt`, `git diff --quiet ...`); "an existing failing test" (`13` §13.2 step 2's first preference) cannot be run by REPRODUCE, and the PROVE re-run of the reproduction has the same limit (the layer check is FORGE's own `forge test run`, so a fix can still be proved). Widening (`pnpm test*`, `node *`) is the owner's decision and belongs with P15's grant work; every widening is still bounded by the operator veto, containment, network and the scrubbed environment. Also disclosed: `git *` is inherently broad (in the lane it still allows `git checkout`, `git reset --hard`, `git clean` and, through history, `git log -p` shows a secret that was committed and later removed; the remedy for that is rotation, `20` §20.4). Also, `rg --hidden/-u/--no-ignore` and `git grep --no-index` are refused (they read what git and ripgrep skip, which is where `.env` lives). Every existing `debug.test.ts` scenario now declares the exec patterns its proposed command needs on the FIXTURE agent (`RCA_EXEC`), as a project would; no shipped agent changed.

**D3. Taint restriction (`20` §20.5 points 3-4; the spec names the actions, not an exact grant).** A step with `taint: 'external'` gets, in `compileSession` (`restrictGrantForTaint`, one place for every dispatch path): `read` kept; `exec` removed (a permitted `git`/`rg` still has flags that write or execute, so a shorter list is not enough); `network: 'none'` with its host list; the adapter-specific `extra` tools dropped; `write` kept only when the step has somewhere to write (`resolveStepClaim(...).globs` non-empty, or the caller confines writes itself: `callerConfinesWrites`, used by `forge debug`'s FIX); the prompt's constraint block states the restricted grant and shows `git_commit: none` / no deploy; and the claim is enforced `strict` at every autonomy level (`resolveStepClaim`). Conservative reading, recorded as an owner decision. Consequences: (a) a tainted panel synthesis or debate decider keeps NO write access it did not need (Q203 D8), and one that declares `produces`/`outputs` keeps write only there; (b) `forge debug`'s FIX has no exec now (it had the diagnostician's `git *`/`cat*` since P27); the loop runs the tests for it; (c) no shipped workflow declares a `panel`/`debate` `mode:`, so no shipped step changes today; `forge panel` and ad-hoc sessions have no claim, so their synthesis writes nothing; (d) the FIX phase is tainted STRUCTURALLY (`assembleDebugSession`: always, whether or not the loop attached data to the request; only the preflight, which exists to read the resolved grant, is untainted); nothing outside `forge debug`, the panel/debate dispatch and the read-only interaction path sets `taint` today (`StepNode.taint`'s own comment still says so), so no workflow step is restricted yet; (e) `15` §15.5.4's "write ADRs without human confirmation" is NOT enforced (a debate decider whose step declares an ADR output still writes it): needs the human-confirmation flow of `20` §20.3, a product decision.

**D4. The FIX claim is stated as an exclusion, over git's own listing (`engine/rca/fix-scan.ts`, `cli/commands/loop/lane-guard.ts`).** `13` §13.2 step 7 says "minimal, must not touch unrelated code", not where. `Defect.affected` names CAP/STORY ids, the ISOLATE scope is model text, and P14's `enforceClaim` holds a step to a POSITIVE glob list (`matchesAnyGlob` is `some`, so `!negation` cannot express "everything except"). So the claim is "ordinary source and test files anywhere, except the protected set". The scan reads `git diff --cached --raw -z --no-renames` (NUL-separated records: a name git quotes, a `"`, a non-ASCII byte, cannot hide a file; a first critic round broke a header-parsing first draft this way), each file's new mode and its ADDED text (`-U0 --text`, so a binary is scanned as text and a line beginning `++ ` is content, not a header), and the ignored files present. Refused: `.git`, `.forge/**`, `**/.env*`, `**/node_modules/**`, key and credential files (`*.pem *.key id_rsa* .npmrc .netrc .aws/ .ssh/ secrets.local.yaml`), CI and hook configuration (`.github/`, `.husky/`, `.circleci/`, `.gitlab-ci.yml`, `Jenkinsfile`, `.gitattributes`, `.gitmodules`), files the project's tooling EXECUTES when it runs the tests (`**/package.json`, `.yarnrc*`, `.pnpmfile.cjs`, `.envrc`, `Makefile`, `.cargo/`, `lefthook.yml`, `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, `vitest|jest.config.*`, `.mocharc*`), the project's document roots (`paths.kb|specs|sessions|reports`); a symlink (`120000`) or submodule (`160000`); a secret-shaped ADDED line (`SECRET_PATTERNS` plus `sk-ant-`, `AIza`, PGP/OPENSSH key blocks, live payment keys, npm tokens; never quoted back); and any ignored file (`git add -A` never lists one, and `git clean -fd` between attempts leaves it, so the tests would execute it: `resetLaneBeforeSession` now also runs `git clean -fdx`). It runs on every FIX attempt **before PROVE** (which runs the project's tests against the diff, i.e. executes it) and again on the exact diff about to be committed (`RUN-096` thrown if that one ever fails). A violation refuses the whole attempt (not trimmed), is not tracked as `fixState.lastDiff`, is recorded as `refused (RUN-096: <rule>: <path> (<detail>))` in `fixAttempts`, and emits `PolicyViolation {kind: 'fix-diff-refused'}`. A session that writes only ignored files produces an empty diff, so no PROVE runs; that path is safe. `taint` and the FIX claim: the FIX session keeps `write` (`callerConfinesWrites`) because the scan IS its claim; it is not P14's `enforceClaim` (no positive globs exist), and that is stated, not hidden.

**D4b. FORGE's own git calls in the lane (`lane-guard.ts`).** The lane's `.git` is a plain file pointing at the real git directory, and the FIX session can write in the lane. A `.git` the session replaced with a repository of its own (`core.fsmonitor` set to a script) makes the next `git add -A` FORGE runs execute that script, with FORGE's environment, before any scan (a first critic round reproduced this). Every git call FORGE makes in the lane now goes through `LaneGuard`: the `.git` pointer is restored first and a changed one refuses the attempt (`protected-path: .git`), the environment is the scrubbed one, `core.fsmonitor=false` and `core.hooksPath=/dev/null` are passed for the call, argv only, `--literal-pathspecs`, `--no-ext-diff --no-textconv`, `--binary` on the diff that is applied at commit time (a binary change used to fail `git apply` after PROVE). Reset and commit go through the guard too (`LaneGuard.reset`: `git reset --hard` then `git clean -ffdxq`, which removes ignored files and nested repositories and, if a directory the tests made read-only stops it, makes the lane writable once and retries; `LaneGuard.commit`: the index the scan just staged (a file written after the scan is not committed), `--no-verify`, `core.hooksPath` and `core.fsmonitor` off, `commit.gpgsign` stated either way, the user's git config and `GIT_AUTHOR_*`/`GIT_COMMITTER_*` kept for identity, the signing agent's variables only when signing); every other guarded call reads neither the user's nor the system's git config, so a `.gitattributes` `filter=` from the user's config cannot run on session-written files. `debug.ts` no longer calls `commitInLane` or `resetLaneWorktree`; the cleanup in `finally` is best effort so it cannot replace the run's outcome. A test replaces `.git` with an fsmonitor repository and shows a plain `git add -A` runs the script (control) and the guarded path does not.

The protected set also covers editor and agent-tool auto-execution (`.claude/`, `.mcp.json`, `.vscode/`, `.devcontainer/`, `.cursor/`) and other CI vendors, matched case-insensitively at any depth.

**D5. The environment.** Allowlist, not blocklist (§2). `HOME` is kept because builds need it; files under it (`~/.aws`, `~/.ssh`) are therefore readable by PROJECT code that runs, but not through a proposed command (`secret-path`/`path-escape`/`expansion` refuse `~` and `$HOME`). `forge test run` and the revert check (`engine` origin) also run scrubbed: a test suite that needs a variable the allowlist omits fails visibly, and the fix is one line in `CONFINED_ENV_ALLOWLIST`.

### 4. Tests written first, from the spec text

- `engine/test/dispatch/confined-command.test.ts` (138): a 60-row hostile matrix (each command with the reason it is refused), the denylist over a `*` grant, an exact pattern with an operator, symlink escape and non-escape, 14 allowed read-only reproductions, network `full` and `allowlist`, the environment allowlist (a canary in the REAL process environment is invisible to the child; `env`/`printenv` show none), stdin closed, cwd, timeout with a grandchild, output cap on both streams, no leaked exit listener, and a canary file that no refused command creates.
- `engine/test/rca/shell.test.ts` (7), `engine/test/rca/loop.test.ts` (+7: a refusal is not a reproduction, five refused attempts end `needs-more-evidence` with `refusedCommands`, the refusal reaches the next prompt, a killed command is not a reproduction, PROVE with a refused reproduction is not proved, the origin of each command, a refused FIX diff never reaches PROVE).
- `engine/test/rca/fix-scan.test.ts` (52), `cli/test/commands/loop/lane-guard.test.ts` (14: real git, quoted and non-ASCII names, `+++` content, binary, ignored files, a replaced `.git` with `core.fsmonitor` (with a control showing plain git runs it), shared-gitdir hook and fsmonitor on reset/commit, gpgsign, read-only directory), `engine/test/security/taint-grant.test.ts` (14: the pure rule; the grant the adapter RECEIVES through `executeStep` and `dispatchAgentStep` panel and debate, against an untainted control; the prompt text; strict claim at a `warn` default).
- `engine/test/plan/command-quoting.test.ts` (70, incl. refused contexts and backslash/comment states), `test/command-steps-quoting.test.ts` (23: every shipped `run:` rendered with and without quoting, from the real workflow files): 24 hostile values (`$(..)`, backticks, `;`, `&&`, `||`, `|`, `&`, newline, `'`, `"`, `>`, `$HOME`, `${IFS}`, `*`, `~`, spaces, empty, `-rf`, `#`, `(..)`, unicode) through `stageId`, `defectId`, `vars.*`, `--flag={{x}}`, and a fanout item's `id` and `owner_role`, each RUN in a real `/bin/sh` (the value arrives as one argument, byte for byte, canary absent), also inside `'{{x}}'` and `"{{x}}"`; shipped strings keep their exact text.
- `cli/test/commands/loop/debug-confinement.test.ts` (14), through the real `debugSymptom`, real lane and git, fake adapter: three batches of five hostile REPRODUCE commands under the SHIPPED diagnostician's patterns (`curl ... | sh`, `rm -rf /`, `cat ~/.ssh/id_rsa`, `env`, `printenv ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `git push`, `git push --force`, `;`/`&&`/`$()`/`>` with an absolute canary path, `cat /etc/passwd`, `cat .env`, `git -c core.pager=...`, `rg --pre=...`): each refused with `RUN-095` and its reason, canary absent, synthetic secrets in the parent environment never in the result or the event log, one `PolicyViolation` per refusal; a real reproduction that dumps its own `env` to a file (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `SSH_AUTH_SOCK` canaries absent, `PATH` present, cwd the lane); six FIX diffs refused on every attempt (CI workflow, `.forge/config.yaml`, `.env`, a KB document, an AWS-shaped literal, a real fix plus `.husky/pre-commit`) with a `forge` probe on `PATH` proving PROVE never ran and every lane branch still at the base; a control where the clean fix IS proved.
- `test/shell-sinks-inventory.test.ts` (5): every production file under `packages/` that starts a shell or imports `node:child_process` is in the pinned inventory; the detector's own lines; `debug.ts` is not a sink.
- No real API key anywhere; the canaries are synthetic (`canary-value-of-<NAME>`, an AWS-shaped `AKIA` + sixteen letters).

**Existing tests changed, and why (not weakened).** `debug.test.ts`: every fixture diagnostician now declares `RCA_EXEC` (`test -f *`, `true`, `false`), because a proposed command must be in the agent's grant; the P27 hostile-text test used `false # <forged end marker> <injection>` as the command, which is now refused (a `#` comment and `<`/`>`), so the first proposal stays hostile and is asserted where it now travels (the fenced `prior-attempts` block of the next attempt, marked `[refused (shell-operator)]`) while an ordinary command drives the later phases; the FIX-grant test asserts the taint clamp. `forge-debug-real-project.test.ts`: the reproduction is `cat does-not-exist.txt` (matches the shipped `cat*`), and FIX asserts `write` kept, `exec: false`, `network: none`. `helpers.ts`: `writeFixtureAgent` takes an optional `exec`. `debug*.test.ts`/the real-project test pass `env: process.env` (`DebugDeps.env`).

### 5. Interpolation (`engine/expr/template.ts`, `engine/plan/compile.ts`)

`resolveTemplate(template, context, { escapeValue })`: the literal text is scanned for the open quote at each placeholder (single, double, or none, honouring backslash escapes), and `shellQuoteValue(value, quoteContext)` escapes for that context: unquoted, a plain token (`[A-Za-z0-9_@%+=:,./-]+`) is left as is, anything else is single-quoted; inside `'...'` only `'` is escaped (`'\''`); inside `"..."` `\ " $` and a backtick are backslash-escaped. Applied ONLY to a `kind: command` step's `run` (compile.ts), the one place a substituted value becomes shell text; branch names, globs, agent ids and briefs are substituted as before. A NUL in a value is refused (`CFG-015`), not truncated. A placeholder that follows a construct the scanner does not model (`$(`, a backtick, `<<`, `$'`, `${`, a comment, or a literal `$` immediately before it) is refused (`CFG-015`, compile issue `template-resolution-failed`) instead of guessed at; no shipped `run:` has one (`test/command-steps-quoting.test.ts` renders every shipped command step, read from the real workflow files, with and without quoting and asserts identical text). Every shipped `run:` string compiles to the same text (they are plain tokens: `test/command-steps.test.ts`, `test/run-inputs-compile.test.ts` and `command-quoting.test.ts` assert it). This is defence in depth beside P21's `RUN-088` (which refuses shell-unsafe `--input` values at parse time and is unchanged): it covers values P21 does not see: story/epic/defect document fields, `vars:` blocks, fanout items, KB and spec fields. Quoting does not stop ARGUMENT injection: a value that starts with `-` still becomes a flag of the command it is an argument to (`RUN-088` refuses that for `--input`; a document field is schema-validated where it is an id).

### 6. Mutation checks (real, restored, verified against the saved copy)

`forge debug` routed through unconfined `runShellCommand`: the three hostile batches and both env tests fail (the commands ran; nothing else had to be broken; note that this mutation executes the hostile commands for real, so it was run once and the matrix's `rm -rf /` is refused by the OS's own `rm` on `/`). `scrubbedEnvironment` returning the parent env: 7 env tests fail across the three files. `restrictGrantForTaint` bypassed in `compileSession`: 7 of 14 taint tests fail. `escapeValue` removed in compile.ts: 34 of 56 quoting tests fail. The loop reading a refusal or a timeout as a reproduction (`if (unusable !== undefined) continue` removed): 3 loop tests fail. The FIX scan disabled in `debug.ts`: all 6 refusal scenarios fail.

### 7. Verification scope (owner-approved cost cut; the full suite was not run)

`packages/engine` (whole: one failure, `e2e/crash-resume.test.ts` timing out under load, the known flake), `packages/cli/test/commands/{loop,run}` (the only failures are 4 in `run/merge.test.ts`, "fixture run left no ready lane", which fail identically on a clean HEAD worktree with none of this piece's changes), `packages/testkit`, `packages/schemas`, `packages/core/test/errors.test.ts`; root `test/{agent-prompts-all-workflows,output-contract-known-gaps,workflows,build-stage-compiles,workspace-floor,fm-service-workflow,fm-mobile-workflow,live-smoke,determinism,command-steps,command-steps-quoting,strict-opt-outs,run-inputs-compile,brief-write-paths-in-claim,forge-debug-real-project,shell-sinks-inventory}.test.ts` (the final scoped run after round 3: `packages/engine`, `packages/cli/test/commands/loop`, `packages/core/test/errors.test.ts` and the root files above: 126 of 127 files pass, the one failure being the known `crash-resume` load flake) (`workspace-floor`'s collected-file count failed once while other agents were adding test files and passes alone); `pnpm typecheck` (package projects clean; the root project's only errors are another piece's in-flight `test/build-stage-lane-landing.test.ts`), `pnpm run boundaries`, eslint and prettier on every file I own.

### 7b. Three critic rounds (fresh subagents, `GAUNTLET-LOG.md`, `## M13 P28`)

Round 1 (4 blocking, 4 major): `git grep --open=` (git accepts any unambiguous prefix of a long option), `git archive --remote` and other remote routes under `network: none`, FORGE's own git calls running with the full environment on a lane the session can write (a replaced `.git` with `core.fsmonitor`), and a diff scan that missed quoted names, `+++` content, ignored files, binaries and execution-config files: all fixed (git allowlist, `LaneGuard`, `--raw -z` parsing). Round 2 (4 blocking, 5 major): `-nO<cmd>` short clusters, `ls=1 node` against prefix patterns, unguarded `commitInLane`/`resetLaneWorktree`, a placeholder after a template backslash, package-manager verbs behind flags, globs reaching secrets, an inventory blind to imports of `node:child_process`: all fixed. Round 3 (1 blocking, 4 major): a glob expanding to an option-shaped file name, a glob through a symlinked directory, a cleanup failure masking the outcome, `commit.gpgsign` in the user's config breaking the guarded commit, editor/agent-tool auto-execution config missing from the protected set, taint of FIX depending on a data-flow condition, an over-refusing glob cap: all fixed; a loop test that could not detect its own bug was strengthened. Three rounds is the limit; findings not fixed are in §8.

### 8. Left open (each for the orchestrator)

- **PROVE is the escape from every restriction on the FIX session.** `forge test run` and the reproduction run the code the FIX wrote, with the network open and the real `HOME`; only the scrubbed environment holds. Detective (scan after the writes), not preventive. An OS sandbox (no network, read-only home) is the fix.
- **Reading history.** `git log -p`, `git show <sha>`, `git cat-file -p <blob>` read secrets committed and later removed without naming a path; the path vet cannot see object addressing (rotate, `20` §20.4). `.env.example` is refused as `.env*` (over-refusal, by the spec's pattern). A reproduction that genuinely hangs is reported as killed, so a deadlock cannot be reproduced by REPRODUCE.
- **The engine environment allowlist is narrow** (`VOLTA_HOME`, `NVM_DIR`, `JAVA_HOME`, `CARGO_HOME`, `XDG_*`, proxy and CA variables are not passed): a test suite that needs one fails visibly and PROVE escalates; no per-project passthrough exists yet.
- **`refusedCommands` is in the `DebugResult` JSON and the `PolicyViolation` events, not in the recorded RCA document** (the `rcaSchema` has no field for it).
- **`forge debug` installs no interrupt handler**: Ctrl-C can orphan the detached process group of a running `forge test run` (bounded by the 20-minute limit).
- **Template quoting stops shell injection, not option injection or word splitting**: a value starting with `-` is still a flag; `echo $HOME{{y}}` extends a variable name (a literal `$` right before a placeholder is refused, a `$NAME` immediately before it is not); nothing models `cmd.exe`.
- **`revertCheckScript`** (a race-condition proof) runs shell `git` in the lane after PROVE ran session code, unguarded; and it checks `HEAD~1` of a lane whose fix is not yet committed (pre-existing).

- **Two untrusted-source sinks still run with no grant, no denylist and no scrub:** `forge adopt` phase 5 (`engine/adopt/verification.ts`: commands derived from the brownfield repository, in a sandbox clone, with the whole environment) and `forge kb verify` (`cli/commands/kb.ts`: a command stored in a KB entry, in the live tree, with the whole environment). A stored command should pass the same `vetProposedCommand`/`runConfinedCommand`; whether adopt may run an untrusted repository's build at all is a product decision (`17` §17.2 phase 5 says it does).
- **Not a sandbox.** The network policy refuses a `curl` and a `git push`; it cannot refuse a script that opens a socket. PROVE (`forge test run`) executes whatever code the FIX wrote, with the network and the user's files; the scrubbed environment keeps secrets out of the process environment, not off the disk. Only an OS-level sandbox (no network, a read-only home) closes that; the scan lowers the odds and records the attempt. `package.json` scripts and test files are ordinary files a fix may change.
- **Workflow `command` steps and gate checks are author-trusted**, not confined to a grant, and run with the parent environment plus `commandEnv`. That is by design (the project's own commands), but a module or overlay is a third party's text; `forge audit`/overlay review is where that is caught.
- **The shipped diagnostician's exec patterns** (D2) and the broad `git *`: owner decision, with P15.
- **`15` §15.5.4 "write ADRs without human confirmation"** for a tainted step (D3d).
- **Two copies of the kill-the-group logic** (`shell.ts`'s limited runner, added by P25, and `confined-command.ts`): collapse them once P25 has landed.
- The `RUN-093`/`RUN-094` numbers are unused (reserved when this piece chose its codes).

**Gauntlet:** see `GAUNTLET-LOG.md`, `## M13 P28`. Files: `packages/engine/src/dispatch/{confined-command,assemble,outputs}.ts`, `packages/engine/src/rca/{shell,fix-scan,loop,types,index}.ts`, `packages/cli/src/commands/loop/lane-guard.ts`, `packages/engine/src/security/{taint-guard,index}.ts`, `packages/engine/src/expr/{template,index}.ts`, `packages/engine/src/plan/compile.ts`, `packages/cli/src/commands/loop/debug.ts`, `packages/cli/src/bin.ts` (`env` in `buildLoopDepsForProject`), `packages/core/src/errors/codes.ts` (`RUN-095`, `RUN-096`), and the tests above.

## Q221 — M13 P19: lane visibility — the gap was real, a lane no `merge` step lands is integrated by the engine, lanes branch from the integration tip, a `merge` lands the lanes of the work it merges, inline steps and gates read one tree

**Context.** `PLAN-M13.md` P19, owner decision 2026-09-20 (Q3, "yes, after confirming": auto-integrate a successful lane no explicit `merge` step consumes, later lanes branch from the integration tip, explicit `merge` steps and their review-before-merge order untouched), `P11-TRIAGE.md` Break 4 / D2, and the two items Q211 left open (2: which lanes the runtime merge handler merges; 3: a dependent story's chain branches before its dependency is merged), plus Q206 (inline steps run at `projectRoot` while gates read the integration worktree) and Q217 (swarm-review perspectives read the project checkout).

**1. The gap was real (the confirmation the owner asked for).** `packages/engine/test/run/lane-integration.test.ts` was written first, from `06` §6.4 rule 4 / §6.4 lane lifecycle step 4 ("on success -> enqueue in merge queue") and `10` §10.1, against the engine as it stood, real git, real integration worktree laid out the way `forge run` lays one out, fake adapter (strict prompt check on). Of its first 15 tests 13 failed: (a) a two-step chain with no merge step: step two's lane did not contain step one's file and nothing reached the integration branch (`git show HEAD:one.txt` on `forge/integration/current` failed; `main` and the integration branch never held it); (b) an inline `command` step (`test -f docs/epic.md`, run at the project root) and a `gate` whose check reads `docs/epic.md` (run at the integration worktree) read different trees, so the inline step failed although the file was in a lane; (c) parallel lanes, the conflict policies, the no-change lane, an explicit merge landing the `implement` lane and the inline read-only guard all failed for the same reason or because there was no behaviour to assert. The two that passed were the ones that were already right (a failed step's lane is not integrated; a step that only writes ignored state leaves the tree alone). Root cause, read before building: `packages/cli/src/commands/run/context.ts` passed `integrationBase = 'main'` (lanes branched from the trunk, never from what earlier lanes had integrated); only `runMergeStep` ever called the merge queue; `runCommandStep` ran an inline step at `ctx.projectRoot` while `runGateStep` and the queue used `ctx.integrationPath`. So the condition holds for every case the brief listed and nothing was built for a case that was not broken.

**2. What is integrated, when, and how (the engine).** After every scheduling tick (`driveToCompletion`), before the next `scheduler.next()`, `runEngine` sweeps the plan's nodes in plan order (`integrateSucceededLanes`): a node whose step SUCCEEDED (scheduler status, so a failed step's lane, which `runLaneLifecycle` does not register and which resume re-registers as `ready`, is never integrated), which has a registered lane, and which no `merge` lands (section 4), is integrated by `integrateLane` (`dispatch/integrate.ts`). One call site, not a second merge implementation: `landLane` is the body `runMergeStep` had for one predecessor lane (`MergeQueued` -> `MergeStarted` -> `mergeQueue.process` -> `MergeCompleted`/`MergeConflict`/`MergeReverted` or a failure as data, then `removeLane` + `LaneRemoved` + registry delete), moved out and called by both; the queue is still `enqueueForIntegrationPath` (serialised per integration path). Why between ticks and in plan order rather than inside each step: a tick drains completely before the next starts (`driveToCompletion`), so the lanes of one tick integrate one at a time in a fixed order (whichever session finishes first does not decide who merges first and so who conflicts; tested with an `a` that finishes last), a lane of tick N is in the tip every lane of tick N+1 branches from, and a RESUMED run integrates the lanes its predecessor finished but did not get to (`resumeRun` re-registers every `ready` lane) before scheduling anything. Conflict policy: the config's `execution.conflictPolicy` (`RunEngineContext.conflictPolicy`, passed by `buildRunEngineContext`; the engine default `abort`); `agent`/`human` need a resolver on the merge queue, which no production caller wires (Q77), so on the shipped default (`agent`) a real conflict fails the step as `VCS-MISSING-CONFLICT-RESOLVER` data, exactly as it does for an explicit merge today. No pre/post-merge check set: those are a `merge` step's declared `policy` (see Left open). A lane with nothing to land (its step changed no file, so its branch never left its base; or a crash left it merged but not removed) is detected by `MergeQueueFacade.isIntegrated` (`git merge-base --is-ancestor <lane branch> HEAD` in the integration worktree, serialised with the queue) and only removed: no commit, no `Merge*` events, one `LaneRemoved`. A lane that cannot be integrated FAILS its step: `scheduler.markFailed`, a `StepFailed` event with the failure after the earlier `StepSucceeded` (the last terminal event wins on resume), so its dependents never run and the run is `failed`; the lane is kept for inspection (`forge merge` can land it once the cause is fixed). A `TelemetryError` is `RUN-038`, as in `executeStep`.

**3. Lanes branch from the integration tip.** `buildRunEngineContext` now passes `integrationBase = <the integration branch>` (was `'main'`; the trunk only seeds the branch the first time it is created), the branch `integrationPath` has checked out, which is what `ExecuteStepContext.integrationPath` always documented ("an existing worktree already checked out on `integrationBase`"). `runLaneLifecycle` creates the lane FROM THE SHA IT JUST RESOLVED (`createLane(node.id, baseSha)`, not the branch name again): the branch moves during a run now, and a lane created from a newer tip than the `baseSha` its claim is enforced against would show other lanes' files as its own out-of-claim writes and `strict` would revert them out of the lane (a critic found this race; tested by advancing the branch between the two calls). Only workflow runs do this (`lanesFromIntegration`, set by `runWorkflow` and `resumeWorkflow`): `forge review`, `debug`, `session` and `panel` build a context too, integrate nothing and want the code as it is on `main`, so they keep `integrationBase = 'main'` (a round-2 critic: the integration branch only moves when a run lands lanes and is never re-synced, so a review lane based on it would read stale source). The integration branch is named by the run's stage: the config's `execution.integrationBranch` (`forge/integration/{stage}`) with `{stage}` replaced by the run's `stageId` input when it is a safe identifier (`integrationBranchFor`, `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`, no `..`, 64 characters, else `current`), from the run's expression context in `runWorkflow`, from the manifest's recorded context in `resumeWorkflow` and in `forge merge` (`integrationBranchOfRun`; a manifest that cannot be read is `RUN-054`, not a guess). The config is the single source of truth (`18` §18.3); a workflow's own `vars.integration_branch` is NOT followed (an earlier draft did, and a round-3 critic showed it splits a project whose template is customised: `plan-stage` has no var and would integrate elsewhere). Why the stage is in the name: `build-stage`'s `prepare` step (`git switch -c {{vars.integration_branch}} || git switch ...`, `vars.integration_branch = forge/integration/{{stageId}}` since P21) runs in the integration worktree now (section 6); with the default template the run's branch is that branch and `prepare` has nothing to switch. A project that customises the template must customise that var too: otherwise `prepare` switches the integration worktree, the inline guard reverts it and fails `prepare` naming the change (tested; the integration branch stays intact). Also fixed, found by `resume.test.ts` (a real SIGKILL): `ensureIntegrationWorktree` returned a directory a killed `git worktree add` had left half-made (`locked initializing`, no `commondir`/`HEAD`, or an empty directory that git resolves to the project's own repository) as if it were healthy; nothing used that tree before, everything does now, so it is checked (top level is the directory itself, `HEAD` resolves, git lists it) and discarded and made again otherwise (tested with both leftovers).

**4. "Consumed by a merge", defined from the compiled DAG (`plan/merge-scope.ts`).** `mergeLandingScope(nodes, mergeId)`: every step the merge transitively waits for (`dependsOn`, which is where a fanout merge's `over` lands after compilation, Q211 1), EXCEPT the integration checkpoints upstream of it and everything upstream of those: a `gate` or another `merge`. `stepsLandedByMerges` is the union over the plan's merge nodes; a lane not in it is the engine's to integrate. This is the literal rule ("a merge whose dependency closure includes the lane's step") plus one refinement, and it is the one decision here the owner may want to veto: a lane upstream of a checkpoint that is itself upstream of the merge is integrated before the checkpoint. Why the refinement is needed and not a preference: `build-stage` compiles `freeze-contracts -> contracts-gate -> [generate-tests -> implement -> review]* -> merge`, and the compiler adds `implement -> freeze-contracts` directly (`06` §6.6 contract-first dependency), so `freeze-contracts` IS in the merge's closure by the literal rule; deferred to the end it would leave `contracts-gate` (reads the integration worktree) and every story lane (`inputs: artifact:InterfaceContract(*)`) with no contract to read. The test proves it on the shipped graph (`stepsLandedByMerges` excludes `freeze-contracts`; the real run below shows the story sessions see the contract). It is "behind a checkpoint on SOME path", not "reached without crossing one", because of that implicit edge. Consequence, stated in the spec bullet: a gate placed between an `implement` step and its `review` integrates `implement` before the review (the gate has to read it); no shipped workflow does that. Lanes of steps in no merge's closure (every step of a workflow with no merge, and steps after the last merge) are integrated as they succeed.

**5. `runMergeStep`'s predecessor semantics (Q211 item 2).** A merge lands the lanes of every step in its landing scope, dependencies first (post-order over `dependsOn`, each list in the order it names them), not merely its direct predecessors' lanes; for the shipped `build-stage` that is, per story, `generate-tests`, `implement`, `review` (the `REVIEW-NNN.md` the engine wrote) and the stories in story-dependency order. Reading of `06` §6.5 / `10` §10.1 ("merge-queue processing for a *set* of lanes"): what has to reach the integration branch is what the review approved. The plan is `ExecuteStepContext.stepGraph`, set by `runEngine` (a copy of the context sharing every field including the lane registry); a merge driven with no plan (a bare handler in a unit test) lands its direct `dependsOn` lanes as before, which a test pins (`the pre-P19 behaviour, kept for a bare handler`). Two further rules the round-1 critic showed were needed once the scope is a closure: the lanes of one merge are CLAIMED up front (taken out of the registry in the same synchronous step that chose them, put back when they did not land), so two merges in one tick whose scopes share an upstream lane (two merges over disjoint reviews building on one lane) land it once; and a lane whose own dependency lane did not land (`MERGE-DEPENDENCY-NOT-LANDED`) is not landed either (a review report for code that is not there), while independent lanes carry on (`detail.merges` still has every outcome, the first failure is the step's). A lane with nothing to land is not merged by a  step either ( asks  first: git reports "already up to date" and makes no commit, so the step would log a  carrying another lane's merge commit, and a failing post-merge check would revert THAT lane's merge; found by a round-3 critic). A removal that fails after a lane landed is not a step failure (a  event, the lane left on disk, the run goes on): the work is integrated, and failing the step would kill the run over a leftover worktree.

**6. Inline steps and gates read the integration worktree; an inline step may not change it (`dispatch/inline-tree.ts`).** `06` §6.2 says `inline` is "run in supervisor, no worktree" and `10` §10.1 "runs in the supervisor, else in a lane": no tree is named, and the module workflows say what is meant ("the 'run directly against the current integration state' case `inline` exists for", `contract-test-cycle`, `store-release`). Gates already read `integrationPath` (`runGateStep`, Q62). So an inline `command` step now runs at `ctx.integrationPath` (was `projectRoot`), the one tree that holds what earlier lanes produced, which is what lets `derive-run-plan` (`forge plan run-plan`) see the Epics and Stories `write-epics`/`write-stories` created. That tree belongs to the merge queue: a merge into a tree with local changes fails and a tree moved to another branch merges into the wrong one, so "read-only inline steps must not dirty it" is enforced, not trusted: snapshot before (HEAD, branch, non-ignored `git status -z` entries), run, restore after: a switched branch or moved HEAD is put back (`checkout --force`, `reset --hard`), a new untracked path is removed, a modified or added tracked path is restored from HEAD (`--literal-pathspecs`), and the step FAILS naming what it touched (`INLINE-CHANGED-INTEGRATION-TREE`; a step that also exited non-zero reports its own failure with the reverted changes appended). Ignored paths (`.forge/state/`, build output the project ignores) are free. The whole snapshot-run-restore window is one `MergeQueueFacade.exclusive` operation (the merge queue's own per-path chain): without it a merge landing in the same tick would be undone by the restore's `reset --hard` (a critic showed it; tested with a `sleep 1` inline step beside an explicit merge). A step that needs to write files belongs in a lane. Interrupted git operations (a process killed inside the merge queue's /Already up to date.) are abandoned before the next attempt: the merge queue facade aborts a rebase in the lane and a merge in the integration worktree, and  aborts a rebase in each of the run's lanes before its orphan reclaim (a lane mid-rebase has a detached HEAD, so the reclaim took its branch for an orphan and tried to delete a checked-out branch). Not serialised: gate checks (a gate that writes into the tree it reads is its own concern; a human-approval wait must not hold the queue).

**7. Q211 item 3 (a dependent story's chain branches before its dependency is merged): NOT applied, an owner decision.** Inside one merge's scope (`generate-tests -> implement -> review` of a story, and story B after story A) lanes still branch from a tip that does not hold their dependency's code, by the owner's own constraint that a lane a merge consumes is not integrated before that merge (review-before-merge). The spec does not say how a chain inside a merge's scope sees its predecessor: `06` §6.4 says lanes branch "from the integration branch", nothing else. Options (each needs the owner; none is a spec change I can justify): (a) a lane whose sole `dependsOn` predecessor is an unmerged lane branches from THAT LANE'S tip (stacked lanes; the merge still lands the chain in order, review-before-merge preserved, no DSL; joins of several lanes need a merge of lanes first); (b) per-story `merge` steps (a fanout of merges, `06` §6.5's queue per lane) so a story's dependents branch after it landed: workflow authoring, and the compiler's per-item folding (Q211 1) would have to change; (c) integrate every lane whose step is followed only by lanes of the same story after its `review` verdict (needs the review verdict to gate something, which nothing does yet, Q217 found (a)). My recommendation: (a). Until one is chosen `implement` does not see `generate-tests`' tests in the shipped `build-stage`, and `implement-story`'s `red`/`green` do not see `plan`'s record: the inner loops need it before a live run.

**8. Swarm-review perspectives (Q217 known limitation): disclosed, not changed.** The perspectives still run with `cwd = ctx.projectRoot`. With this change the reviewed work is NOT reachable from the integration tip (it sits in the `implement` lane the merge lands after `review`), so pointing the sessions at the integration worktree would not show them the diff either; the honest fix is option 7(a) (the review lane based on the implement lane). The report already says which checkout the perspectives read.

**Tests written first (from the spec text) and mutation evidence.** Engine (`packages/engine/test/run/lane-integration.test.ts`, 27, real git and events, `runEngine` over parsed YAML): the chain and inline+gate confirmations; parallel lanes in plan order however they finish (one is slowed); a no-change lane leaves no commit and no `Merge*` event; a failed step's lane; conflicts under `abort` (MergeConflict, first lane kept, tree clean), `agent` without a resolver (failure as data, tree clean) and `agent` with a resolver (resolved and integrated); an explicit merge untouched (review does not see implement; the merge lands both; every Merge event belongs to the merge step); a gate between an agent step and a later merge is a checkpoint; the inline guard (cwd, new file removed, tracked file restored, branch switch and commit undone, file with a space, a failing step reports its own failure, ignored state free); concurrency in one tick (inline vs merge, two merges sharing a lane, a dependent of a lane that did not land, the base race); crash/resume at `MergeQueued`, `MergeStarted`, `MergeCompleted`, `LaneRemoved` (a fresh `resumeRun` + `runEngine` with a new context: the lane lands exactly once, step one is not run again, step two sees its output) a lane killed mid-rebase, a lane whose removal fails after it landed, an explicit merge over a no-change lane, and a failed step's re-registered lane. `plan/merge-scope.test.ts` (9).
