Root `test/build-stage-lane-landing.test.ts` (6): the SHIPPED `build-stage` compiled with two stories, its real nodes driven through `executeStep` (real lanes, merge queue, output contract, the engine-written swarm-review report): the merge integrates the implement and generate-tests lanes and both reports, in dependency order; a merge with no plan lands only review lanes (the pre-fix behaviour); and the shipped source through `runEngine` up to `deliver` (the engine refuses subworkflows, RUN-039) with a stage context and the stage branch: the contract lane is integrated before the gate and before any story session (each sees it), the story lanes land at the merge, `prepare` is a no-op. CLI: `context.test.ts` (a workflow run's base is the integration branch and an ad-hoc command's stays , the stage names the branch, config is the single source, unsafe ids never reach a ref, a half-made worktree is remade, a worktree left on another branch or mid-merge is repaired in place and not discarded), `lane-integration.test.ts` (a chain through `runWorkflow`; a stage run's `prepare`). Existing assertions that encoded the bug, changed and why: `context.test.ts` `integrationBase` was `'main'`; `status.test.ts` "the lane left ready by a merge-less run" is now `removed` (the engine integrated it); `merge.test.ts` needed a real `ready` lane and got it from a merge whose pre-merge check fails (the case `forge merge` exists for) instead of from a merge-less run. Mutations, each reverted after: sweep disabled -> 13 of 20 engine + the CLI chain test fail; `runMergeStep` on direct predecessors -> 4 (engine explicit-merge, gate-cutoff, two build-stage); inline at `projectRoot` -> 2; inline restore removed -> 3; lane base `main` in `buildRunEngineContext` -> the context test and the CLI chain test; merge scope without the checkpoint exclusion -> 6; sweep without the scheduler-status check -> the re-registered failed lane is integrated (1); `isIntegrated` not consulted -> the no-change case and crash-at-`MergeCompleted` (2); no `exclusive` -> the inline-vs-merge test; no up-front claim -> the shared-lane test; no dependent skip -> the dependent test; `createLane` from the branch name -> the base race test; the CLI's stage id not passed -> the stage `prepare` test.

**Left open (found here, not fixed; each is its own piece or an owner call).** (a) The shipped `build-stage` merge declares `preChecks: fast` / `postChecks: full` (`10` §10.1's example), which the engine runs as shell commands (`fast: command not found`, `MERGE-PRE-CHECK-FAILED`): a real `build-stage` merge lands nothing until the names resolve to real check sets (config) or the policy names commands. The tests swap the policy for `{conflict: abort}` and say so. (b) Auto-integrated lanes have no pre/post-merge check set (`06` §6.5 steps 3 and 5): there is nowhere a run declares one for a lane no merge names; options: a config key (`execution.mergeChecks: {pre, post}`) applied to every candidate, or leave checks to `merge` steps. (c) The default `execution.conflictPolicy` is `agent` and no resolver is wired: any two lanes touching one file (a lockfile, a changelog, `sharedMutablePaths`) end the run at integration with `VCS-MISSING-CONFLICT-RESOLVER` (Q77); it was already true of explicit merges, and is now reachable by every multi-step workflow. (d) The integration branch is never re-synced with `main` across runs (it accumulates); lanes used to see `main`'s newer commits, they now see the integration branch. A fast-forward of an unmerged-into-nothing integration branch to `main` at run start, or a documented `deliver` step, is the fix. (e) A gate can still read a tree a concurrent merge is changing (only inline steps are serialised with the queue). (f) A crash between `git merge` and the `MergeCompleted` event leaves `MergeStarted` with no completion for that lane; resume removes the lane (`isIntegrated`) and does not invent an event (the merge commit's sha is not known there). (g) `resumeRun` treats a `ready` lane whose worktree is gone as merged (`existsSync`); with the sweep as the only integration path of a merge-less workflow that assumption is load-bearing: check `merge-base --is-ancestor` on the lane branch when it still exists. A crash mid-rebase inside `processMergeCandidate` leaves the lane worktree rebasing and the resumed integration fails on it (the same for explicit merges). (h) Inline steps run in a fresh worktree: no `node_modules` (a `pnpm test` inline step, `fm-mobile`/`fm-service`, needs the project's install there, as gate checks and post-merge checks already do) and untracked, non-ignored output (`coverage/`) makes a step that exited 0 fail the guard: a project must ignore its build output. (i) Refs an inline step creates (a stray branch after `git switch -c`) are not removed. (j) `standup` (a session step with an empty roster) and `deliver` (a subworkflow, RUN-039) stop the shipped `build-stage` in the engine; the real-run test ends at them. (k) An inline  command runs in the integration worktree, which is its own project root for the CLI (its tracked  is there; the ignored , ,  are not):  (, , , 's ) writes its index under the worktree's ignored , not the project's. That is what reading the integrated tree means, and gates already run there; a workflow that wants the project index rebuilt needs a step that runs at the project root, which the engine has no kind for now. (l) The integration worktree is shared by every process on the project:  and the queue are per process, so a second process (, a second run of the stage) moving HEAD during an inline step's window would have its merge undone by the restore's ; the run lock forbids a second run,  does not take it. A killed inline step's leftover files persist (the next snapshot treats them as the baseline). (m)  now waits up to 4 s for a worktree that a killed  is still finishing (its admin directory holds ), repairs a healthy one (wrong branch, half-done merge) and discards one that stays broken; two  racing on the same target, the known  load flake, still exist (the flake got rarer, not gone). (n) A lane abandoned after its removal failed, or kept after a failed integration, is not reclaimed by  (/ and known). (o)  and  are ad-hoc codes (like the other ), classified by  as tool-error/transient though deterministic; nothing calls the classifier yet (D10). (p) The lane of a failed integration stays  in the log (deliberately:  lists ready lanes), where  §6.4 step 4 says . (q) Two merges in one tick sharing an upstream lane the first fails to land: the second's dependency check is per merge. (r)  lanes and every ad-hoc command keep basing on .

**Verification scope (owner-approved cost cut; no full unscoped suite).** All of `packages/engine/test/{dispatch,run,resume,plan,e2e,interaction,scheduler}`, `packages/cli/test/commands/{run,loop}`, `packages/cli/test/{bin,bin-run-failures}.test.ts` and `commands/doctor`, `e2e`, root `test/{build-stage-lane-landing,build-stage-compiles,workflows,agent-prompts-all-workflows,output-contract-known-gaps,fm-service-workflow,fm-mobile-workflow,live-smoke,determinism,workspace-floor}.test.ts`; `pnpm run boundaries`, root and package `tsc`, `eslint` and `prettier` on every file I own. Failures seen and not mine: `engine/test/dispatch/confined-command.test.ts` (P28's file in flight), `zz-critic-probe*` (another agent's critics), `packages/engine/test/plan/command-quoting.test.ts` typecheck (P21/P28 in flight), `workspace-floor` while those fail `tsc`; load flakes: `engine/test/e2e/crash-resume.test.ts` (passes alone), `cli/test/commands/run/resume.test.ts` (one failure in eight runs before the worktree repair, none in ten after).

**Spec text (quoted).** `06` §6.4 Rules, new bullet: "A lane whose step succeeded and which no `merge` step lands is enqueued in the merge queue by the engine as soon as the step succeeds (between scheduling ticks, in plan order), and lanes are created from the integration branch tip, so a later step, an inline step and a gate see it. A `merge` step lands the lanes of the steps in its dependency closure (not only its direct predecessors), stopping at a `gate` or another `merge`, which are integration checkpoints (a step upstream of a checkpoint is integrated before it, so what a gate reads is there); it batches and orders them and is never bypassed. A lane no `merge` lands has no pre- or post-merge check set of its own (§6.5 steps 3 and 5 are those a `merge` step declares). An inline step runs in the integration worktree, serialised with the merge queue, and must leave it unchanged." `06` §6.2: `laneAffinity` comment "inline = run in supervisor (in the integration worktree), no lane". `10` §10.1 `command` row: "`inline: true` runs in the supervisor (in the integration worktree), else in a lane". `05` §5.5 not touched.

**Gauntlet.** See `GAUNTLET-LOG.md`, `## M13 P19`.

Files: `packages/engine/src/{plan/merge-scope.ts,dispatch/{integrate,inline-tree,vcs-step,steps,types,facades}.ts,run/run-engine.ts,plan/index.ts}`, `packages/cli/src/commands/run/{context,run,resume,index}.ts`, `packages/cli/src/bin.ts` (the `forge merge` lines), `specs/06`, `specs/10`, and the tests named above.

## Q223 — M13 P35: gates fail closed — what a check must show to pass, the exit-code rule, the one command whose output was missing its field, and five gates that can no longer pass without a waiver

**Context.** P25 (Q219) found and did not fix that `evaluateGate` ignored the exit code and `JSON.parse`d stdout, so `failOn: 'errors > 0'` read against an output with no `errors` field was `undefined > 0`, false, and the check passed. A refusal envelope (`{"v":1,"ok":false,"error":{...}}`,
P21's `refusalEnvelopeLine`), a flag-parse refusal, a renamed field, or a crash that printed JSON therefore passed any gate check. `10` §10.3 rule 1 says a failing deterministic check can only be waived, which makes failing closed safe and auditable: a waiver covers it.
`10` §10.3 is silent on exit codes, on missing fields and on refusals; the rules below are the conservative reading, recorded here because the spec does not state them.

**The rule (`packages/engine/src/gates/evaluate.ts`).** A deterministic check passes only if all of these hold, and any other outcome fails with a `reason` naming what was wrong (the result shape, the `failed(...)` helper and the audit trail of `stdout`/`exitCode` are unchanged):
1. The runner did not throw, the parser is supported, stdout parses as one JSON object (as before).
2. *Failure markers.* No `ok` key other than `true` (so `false`, `"false"`, `0`, `null` all fail), no `success: false`, no top-level `error` other than `null`, `false` or `""`. This is the refusal envelope, and every other spelling a program might use for "did not succeed".
3. *`failOn` must be able to show success.* It reads at least one path (a constant such as `false` or `1 > 2` can never fail the gate, so it is refused), and every path it reads resolves to a defined, non-null value. The paths are found by walking the parsed AST from `@forge/engine/expr` (never the source text), on EVERY branch, including the side of `&&`/`||` that would short-circuit, so `errors > 0 && failed > 0` against `{"errors":0}` fails on the missing `failed`. `@forge/engine/expr`'s own contract (a missing path is `undefined`, right for a workflow `when:`) is untouched; the rule is a gate rule.
4. *Types.* An ordering comparison gets two finite numbers or two strings (`"3"` against `0` is a wrong type, not a number); `==`/`!=` compare two primitives of the same type (`evaluate` uses `===`, and compares arrays and objects by identity); a path used as a yes/no value (operand of `!`, `&&`, `||`, or the whole expression) is a boolean; `length()` takes a string or array; `in` searches an array, or a string for a string.
5. *Exit code.* 0 and 1 are the two codes a command that reached a verdict uses (`EXIT_CODES` in `@forge/core/errors`: 0 success, 1 failure, 2 usage, 3..6 and 130 other). Any other code fails whatever the body says. **Exit 1 with a body that does not trip `failOn` is trusted only when the body is a forge envelope (`v: 1`);** any other program that exits 1 beside a clean body is a contradiction (and a crash exits 1, and so does a signal in `runShellCommand`), so it fails. Exit 0 with a failing body still fails (the data wins).
6. `failOn` then evaluates false. When `failOn` itself is true the result has no `reason`, as before.
A check with no `failOn` string fails with a reason (it used to throw out of `evaluateGate`).

**Why exit 1 is a verdict for a forge envelope (the brief asked to prefer FAIL and verify every shipped passing path exits 0).** The verification against the real CLI found a shipped case where "non-zero exit fails" is wrong: `forge test flaky --json` serves G-Stable (`flaky > 0`) and G-Verify's `test:quarantine-cap`
(`quarantined > 5`) with one invocation, and exits 1 for a human whenever ANY test is flaky or the cap is exceeded (its own doc comment says so, it cannot know which gate is asking). A project with two quarantined tests exits 1 and must pass the G-Verify cap. Failing every non-zero exit would have made G-Verify
unpassable for any project with one flaky test, a regression for a well-formed output. `test coverage` and `test run` have the same shape (an exit predicate wider than the one field a `failOn` reads). Changing those commands' exit codes would change what a human running them sees, so the evaluator takes the exit-1 body as the verdict when it is a versioned forge envelope.
Residual risk, stated: a forge command that crashed after printing a `{"v":1,...}` envelope, or a bug that makes a command exit 1 with a clean count, passes; forge commands print their envelope last and crashes print no stdout (the top-level handler prints a stack), and the guard test runs every shipped forge line. `runShellCommand` reports a signal as exit 1 (an existing test pins it), so a third-party non-forge check killed after printing a clean body no longer passes (no `v:1`).

**Decisions.**
1. *The refusal envelope is not changed* (`refusalEnvelopeLine` carries no `errors: 1, failed: 1`). The evaluator is the fix; adding numeric fields to a generic refusal would make it look like a verdict from every command, and P21's envelope tests pin its shape. Its `ok: false` is exactly the marker the evaluator reads.
2. *One command's output was fixed, not the evaluator.* `forge spec validate --json` (G-Design `spec:validate`, `failOn: 'errors > 0'`) printed `{v, documents, missingRequiredEdges, cycles}` with no `errors`, so that check could never fail (P24 covered `spec validate --rule`; the bare form has no rule). It now prints `errors`: one per invalid document error (at least one per invalid document), one per missing required edge, one per cycle, after the spread so nothing overrides it. `packages/cli/src/bin.ts` (`runSpecValidateCommand`). Every other shipped check's real output carries every field its `failOn` reads (the guard proves it).
3. *Waivers are untouched.* A test drives a gate with a refused check, a missing-field check, a clean one and a real failure through `evaluateGate`, `applyWaiver` and `buildGateReport`: the waived report is approved and still lists every failing check.
4. *`test/gates.test.ts` and one `evaluate.test.ts` test were wrong and are changed, explicitly.* `gates.test.ts` scripted `{}` as "every check passes"; it now scripts a well-formed passing body (every field any shipped `failOn` reads at its passing value) and a failing one, and asserts the first check fails with no `reason` (so it fails on data, not on refusal). `evaluate.test.ts` pinned "a nonzero exit code alone never fails a check" with exit 17; it now pins the opposite. The header comment of `gate-family-coverage.test.ts` and the doc of `describeRefusal` said a gate reads an absent field as "not failing"; reworded.
5. *Consumers audited.* `createGateEvaluator` (the run engine), `forge gate check` and `forge gate waive` all go through `evaluateGate`, so they are fixed. `forge story verify` and `dod` compute their own verdicts from exit-coded resolvers and fail closed. The TUI has no verdict logic. No other code computes a `failOn`.

**The guard (`packages/cli/test/commands/gate-fail-closed.test.ts`).** Derives every deterministic check from `templates/checks/*.gate.yaml` and each module's `checks/*.check.yaml`, runs each through the real `runShellCommand` with a `forge` shim on `PATH` (as a gate does, no `-C`) in a fresh `forge init` project committed clean (hand-built project if `init` is refused on the machine), and requires: the rejected lines are exactly the pinned set and each fails; every other line exits 0 or 1, prints a JSON object without `ok:false`, carries every path its `failOn` reads, and gets a REAL verdict (`reason` absent); `flaky` with two quarantined tests (exit 1: G-Stable fails, the G-Verify cap passes); `spec validate --json` on a broken document counts errors and fails; a schema-invalid config and an appended unknown flag fail every check that reads them, at least one because of the new refusal marker, with a sentinel line still passing (so a broken shim cannot make the test vacuous). The lines that do not read config (`spec validate*`, `test coverage --rule acceptance-criteria`) or ignore an unknown flag (also `test flaky`, `test run --rule oracle-lint`) are an explicit allowlist that must print a real `{v:1}` verdict.

**Accepted consequence, stated because it is a behaviour change.** Eleven shipped lines are still rejected by the CLI (pinned; P23: `doctor --rule test-command`; P26: `spec validate --rule version-skew|migration-order-violations|slo-observability-coverage|runbook-coverage`, `spec interfaces --check-frozen`, `diagram validate --gate`, `diagram generate --all --check`, `deploy --dry-run|--rollback-check`). They used to pass through the refusal envelope; they now FAIL, so
G-Design, G-Foundation, G-Integration, G-Operate and G-Deliver cannot be approved on any project without a waiver until P23 and P26 land. That is the correct fail-closed state and the pins say which piece removes each.

**Disclosed, not fixed (each a candidate piece).**
- `forge gate approve <id>` records `GateApproved` without evaluating the gate at all (`gate-commands.ts` `gateApprove`); `10` §10.3 rule 1 says a gate with a failing check cannot be approved, only waived. Pre-existing, not a verdict-computation path, not this piece's.
- Several shipped shell checks pass on "nothing to scan": `bundle:size`, `a11y:audit`, `contract:verify`, `lineage:coverage`, `data-quality:tests` treat a missing directory as an empty list, and `api:breaking-change` swallows a `git diff` failure and falls back to `HEAD`. Their `failOn` could express the requirement (`violations > 0 || filesScanned == 0`); the scripts would need a failure branch. The evaluator cannot know.
- `loadGateRegistry` defaults a gate with a misspelled `checks` key to no checks, which passes vacuously; `evaluate.test.ts` pins the empty-gate pass (GATE-502 is the extensions package's job). `in` does not check element types (`'a' in [1,2]` is quietly false).
- The audit trail records stdout and the exit code only; a crash's stderr is not recorded (rule 4 says "the exact command output"). Human-mode `forge gate check` prints only `passed=false`; the fail-closed reason is in the JSON report.
- `specs/10` §10.3, `docs/authoring-guide.md` and `docs/method-guide.md` do not state the check contract above (exit 0 or 1, one JSON object, the fields `failOn` reads must be present); `15` §15.7's custom-check author meets the new reasons undocumented. No spec text was changed.
- `fixtures/greenfield-service/.forge/checks` holds a stale copy of the G-Verify gate missing its last three checks. `test flaky` with an unparseable config crashes with a stack and empty stdout (fails closed, ungracefully).
- The guard's fresh project falls back silently to a hand-built one where `forge init` is refused (CI without the platform CLI takes the weaker path). The shim is POSIX `sh`.

**Verification scoping (owner-approved cost cut).** Scoped: `packages/engine` (whole), `packages/extensions`, `packages/cli/test/commands/{doctor,run,loop,spec}`, `gate-family-coverage`, `gate-validate`, `kb-rules`, `gate-fail-closed`, and the root `gates`, `command-steps`, `determinism`, `workflows`, `live-smoke`, `fm-mobile-workflow`, `fm-service-workflow`, `build-stage-lane-landing`; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm run boundaries`, eslint and prettier on the changed files. Failures seen in that run and not this piece's (other agents' in-flight work, each present in isolation without my hunks touching them): `expression-context`, `implement`, `swarm-review-step`, `review-report`, `confined-command`, `command-steps` (elicit and re-derive steps), and the known `crash-resume` flake. Mutation checks (each reverted, each failed named tests): the failure-marker check, the whole path/type walk, the exit-code rule (`!== 0` instead of `0 or 1` fails the flaky test), the `v:1` requirement at exit 1, the read-nothing refusal, the `||`/`&&` right-hand walk, the ordering-operand type check, and the `errors` count in `spec validate --json` (fails the guard's presence check).

**Gauntlet.** Three critic rounds, none empty (`GAUNTLET-LOG.md`, `## M13 P35`). Round 1 (1 major-regression, 2 major, several minor): the exit-code rule failed a well-formed `test flaky` pass; a literal-only `failOn` passed; `==`/`!=`, truthiness and marker spellings were type-unsafe; the guard's runner was hand-split and ran each command twice. Round 2 (3 major): exit 1 was trusted for any body (a crash exits 1); the negative guard tests would have passed on the old evaluator, and a stale shim directory (deleted by `afterEach`) made them pass vacuously (my own bug, found by the round); shipped shell checks pass on nothing. Round 3 (2 major, both outside the evaluator): the new `errors` count had no failing-direction test; the five gates that cannot pass. Each fixed or recorded above.


## Q225 — M13 P36: an empty claim means no write — the fail-closed grant, exclusions as a second list, the nine claims, the protected set, and `Story.owner_role` restricted to implementation roles

**Context.** `PLAN-M13.md` P36 (security), `Q220` "left for the orchestrator" and `Q216` `KNOWN_EMPTY_CLAIM`. After P14/P15 many agents hold `tools.write: true`, and `assembleAgentSession` granted a session `write` from the agent alone. A step with no `outputs` and no `produces` (empty claim) under the default `guided`/`warn` could write anywhere and nothing was reverted; and `Story.owner_role` was free text, so an `{{ownerRole}}` step could run an authoring role with write.

**Decisions.**
1. *Fail closed at assembly.* Effective `write` = agent grant AND (the step's claim non-empty OR `callerConfinesWrites`). `assemble.ts`: `resolveStepClaim(...).globs.length > 0`; the only caller that confines writes itself is `forge debug`'s FIX (P28 D4: its diff is scanned against the protected set), which keeps write. Participant and read-only sessions were already `write: false`. Block [6] says `writing or modifying files (no write: this step declares no outputs or produces)` when the agent could write and the claim withheld it; agent YAML grants are untouched. `resolveStepClaim` also makes an empty-claim agent step `strict` at every autonomy level: whatever such a session changed got past the grant (an `exec` allowlist such as `git apply`, an adapter that ignores the grant), so `warn` keeping it would defeat the rule. Spec text (06 §6.7 bullet "An empty claim means no write") says the withheld grant is the first control, not the only one.
2. *Exclusions are a second list, not `!` entries in the matcher.* `enforceClaim`'s matcher (`minimatch`, `{dot:true}`) reads a claim as a UNION: `['**','!.forge/**']` still matches `.forge/x` through `**`. P14 noted this; the brief's "positive-plus-negation" is therefore implemented in the engine, not the matcher: a `produces` entry starting `!` is an exclusion; `resolveStepClaim` returns `{globs, exclude, protectedSet, policy}` and `enforceClaim(handle, base, globs, policy, excludedGlobs = [])` treats an excluded path as out of claim. **An excluded path is reverted under `warn` as well as `strict`** (a denial, not a policy question; critic round 1 found the first draft only reported it under `warn`, contradicting the spec line it wrote). `!{{run.testPaths}}` (a leading `!` on a whole-entry placeholder) splices one exclusion per listed path (`plan/compile.ts`).
3. *The protected set is P28's, exported, not a second list.* `protectedFixGlobs(roots)` (`rca/fix-scan.ts`, already exported from `@forge/engine/rca`) is what `!@protected` expands to: `.git`, `.forge/**`, `**/.env*`, credentials and keys, CI and hook configuration (`.github`, `.husky`, `.gitlab-ci.yml`, `.circleci`, `Jenkinsfile`...), package manifests and test-runner configuration (`package.json`, `vitest.config.*`, `conftest.py`, `pyproject.toml`, `Makefile`...), editor and agent-tool configuration (`.claude`, `.vscode`, `.cursor`, `.mcp.json`...), and the project's four document roots. New: `NEVER_WRITABLE_GLOBS` (`.git`, `**/.git`, `.forge`, `.forge/**`, `**/.env`, `**/.env.!(example|sample|template)`): the head of that set, excluded from EVERY agent step's claim whatever it says, so a story's `files_expected` cannot make them writable (`.env.example` stays writable: a scaffold step writes one, checked against `scaffold-project`'s brief). Doc roots are now glob-escaped in the set (a root `docs/[kb]` is a literal path; critic round 2). Block [6] names the protected set for a step whose claim has `!@protected`, so the agent is told before it works, not left to lose a file to a revert.
4. *The nine claims.* `debug:fix`, `harden:fix-findings`, `migrate:{expand,contract}`, `quick-fix:{write-failing-test,fix}`, `refactor:refactor-code` (no path scope: a defect, a finding, a goal): `produces: ['**', '!@protected']`, "the project less the protected set" (`06` §6.7 spec text). `implement-story:{document,refactor}` (and, through the same edit, `green`; and `build-stage:implement`): `['{{run.filesExpected}}', '!{{run.testPaths}}']` (`{{item.files_expected}}`, `!{{item.test_paths}}` in `build-stage`): the story's files less its tests. `10` §10.6 says the implementer "may not edit test files (enforced by claim)" and `files_expected` lists the test globs too; critic round 1 showed refactor/document/green could edit the tests the red step wrote, and round 2 that `build-stage:implement` still could. `run.filesExpected`/`run.testPaths` are P21's fields (`test/story-*` subset by `isTestPath`). `KNOWN_EMPTY_CLAIM` in `test/brief-write-paths-in-claim.test.ts` is now `[]`; the hygiene test allows `!`-exclusions and a broad glob in a step that also names `!@protected`; the brief-path test now compares with the exclusions applied.
5. *Implementation role, derived.* `isImplementationAgent(agent)` (`@forge/agents/schema`, from the existing `IMPLEMENTATION_OUTPUT_TYPES` = `Code`, `Component`): an agent that declares a source-code output, the derivation `test/agent-outputs-registry.test.ts` already uses for `{{ownerRole}}` (P18). Shipped: `backend`, `base-engineer`, `data-engineer`, `frontend`, `ml-engineer`, `mobile` (asserted from the real files). `cli/src/commands/implementation-roles.ts` reads `.forge/agents/*.yaml` and judges each file independently (a corrupt unrelated file neither counts nor switches the check off; critic round 1); an absent or empty roster means "not judged" (a project with no agents cannot run anything: RUN-056). Enforced: `forge spec validate` for a Story at any status, the `definition-of-ready` rule (G-Ready), `forge run implement-story --story` / `forge implement` (`RUN-097`, new; `RUN-091` for `sdet`/`reviewer` is checked first, unchanged), the stage path (`readStageStories` error finding `owner-role-not-implementation` -> `RUN-090`, `forge plan run-plan` reports it), and `forge doctor`'s `spec-graph`. The message names the allowed roles and the remedy. Spec: `09` §9.3 rule 8. `Story.md`'s placeholder says so.
6. *Spec text changed (quoted).* `06` §6.7, new bullet: "**An empty claim means no write.** An `agent` step that declares neither `outputs` nor `produces` is given no `write` grant, whatever its agent's definition says: the effective `write` is the agent's grant AND a non-empty claim (`20` §20.1), and block [6] of its prompt says so. ... A `produces` entry that starts with `!` is an exclusion, not a glob ... the reserved entry `!@protected` removes the protected set ... Whatever a claim says, an `agent` step's claim never reaches `.git/`, `.forge/` or a `.env` file, and a path a claim excludes is reverted under `warn` as well as `strict`. ..." `20` §20.1 `write` row: "while a step that declares neither outputs nor `produces` has an empty claim and is given no `write` at all (`06` §6.7)" (was "takes the autonomy-default claim policy"). `09` §9.3 rule 8 (above). `05` §5.5 untouched.

**Tests written first, then mutation-checked.** `engine/test/dispatch/empty-claim.test.ts` (28: grant, block [6], `callerConfinesWrites`, tainted, read-only, exclusions, real-lane reverts under both policies, the session that ignores its grant); `test/write-implies-claim.test.ts` (permanent inventory: every agent step of every shipped workflow, hooks and fanout children included, each installed agent copy, `{{ownerRole}}` = any implementer; write implies a non-empty claim); `test/nine-steps-claims.test.ts` (the nine steps through the real `executeStep` on a real git lane over a real `forge init` project, `supervised` and `guided`: in-claim kept, 12 protected paths reverted with `PolicyViolation`, story tests reverted, empty `files_expected` gives no write; `build-stage` claim); `cli/test/commands/run/empty-claim.test.ts` (full-path `runWorkflow`, three autonomy levels); `cli/test/bin-owner-role.test.ts` (real launcher, `-C`, real roster: `forge run implement-story --story`, `forge implement`, stage run, `plan run-plan`, `spec validate`, `definition-of-ready`, a corrupt sibling agent); `cli/test/commands/doctor/spec-graph-owner.test.ts`; `vcs/test/claims.test.ts` (exclusions, warn revert, the union footgun pinned); `engine/test/plan/compile.test.ts` (`!{{...}}` splice). Existing tests changed for the right reason: `output-claim.test.ts` (4 tests asserted the old empty-claim behaviour: now "no grant, nothing to revert" and the `produces` variant for the warn flag; the strict-reverts-everything second line is now `empty-claim.test.ts`), `e2e/prompt-assembly.test.ts` (the sdet step got `produces` so it still writes), `loop/implement.test.ts` (`sre` is not an implementer: `frontend`), the cli fixture agents (`engineer`, `backend`, `frontend` declare a `Code` output). **Mutations (each reverted, `git diff` checked):** grant from the agent alone (`mayWrite = true`): 10 of 29 fail across the engine and cli tests; drop `produces` from `debug:fix`: 7 (inventory, nine-steps, brief-path); drop `!@protected` from `quick-fix:fix`: 3; `!@protected` no longer expands: 20; no `NEVER_WRITABLE` floor: 7; excluded paths not reverted under `warn`: 13; `ownerRoleProblem` returns nothing: 7.

**Critic rounds (fresh subagents, `GAUNTLET-LOG.md`).** Round 1: 7 major. Exclusions only reported under `warn` (fixed: reverted); refactor/document/green could edit tests (fixed, `!{{run.testPaths}}`); `files_expected` could name the protected set (floor for every claim; `.env.*` in the floor); silent loss with no warning (block [6] now names the protected set; loss is still a `PolicyViolation`, see open items); the owner check failed open on one corrupt agent file (fixed); doctor did not pass `agentsRoot` (fixed); `exec` untouched (disclosed, spec worded; second-line test added). Round 2: 4 major, 9 minor. `build-stage:implement` could still edit tests (fixed); empty claim is a silent no-op (disclosed below); the second line was inert under `warn` (fixed: strict for an empty claim); block [6] blamed the protected set on story-scoped steps (fixed: `protectedSet`); doc roots not escaped, floor missing `**/.git` and bare `.forge` (fixed); missing tests for the read-only/empty case (added).

**Left open (the orchestrator turns these into pieces).**
- **An empty claim is a silent no-op success.** A step with no grant that writes nothing succeeds (Q208's failure shape). Two realistic triggers: (a) a project whose `.forge/workflows/*` were laid down by an earlier `forge init` (its nine steps have no `produces`; `forge upgrade` regenerates them, a customised copy does not); (b) a Story whose `files_expected` has no path that `isTestPath` recognises gives `red`/`generate-tests` an empty `produces`. Recommended: `forge workflow validate` and `forge doctor` finding for a write-capable agent step with no claim, and a `story-without-test-paths` plan finding in `RUN_REFUSED_WARNINGS`.
- **Enforcement is only after the fact and only when the adapter reports changed files** (`Q209`, `Q212`): `exec` allowlists (`git apply`) can still change files; an adapter that under-reports, or an agent that commits its own work, skips enforcement. OS-level confinement is the triage's M14 hardening. `strict` reverts and traces, it does not fail the step (P31).
- **Story-scoped steps exclude the tests and the never-writable floor only**, not the rest of the protected set (a story that lists `package.json` may change it), and a broad `files_expected` such as `src/auth/**` still admits co-located `*.test.ts` (the exclusion is the listed test globs). An all-test `files_expected` is a non-empty claim that is entirely excluded.
- `!`-entries in `node.produces` still reach `globsOverlap`/`ready-set` (minimatch reads `!x` as "everything but x", so such a step overlaps every path: conservative, only implement-story's sequential steps carry them today), the skill-hint filter in `pack-for-step.ts` and block [5]'s "only the paths in this step's claim" text. Recommended: hand those consumers the resolved claim, not raw `produces`.
- `!@protected` is "the very list a `forge debug` FIX is held to" for paths only: the FIX scan's symlink and secret-shaped-value checks (`scanLaneDiff`) do not run on a project-wide step's diff.
- `forge resume` re-runs no owner check (a run started before this change resumes with the owner it had); `agentsRoot?` on `SpecCommandContext`/`RunPlanContext` is optional (a caller that omits it does not judge owners; the three shipped callers pass it); an unreadable owner agent file is blamed on the story, not named.
- Stale generated copies: `fixtures/greenfield-service/.forge/workflows/*` and `templates/Story.md` lack the new claims (generated; `test/greenfield-fixture-generated.test.ts` tolerates it).
- I ran `prettier --write packages/engine/src` once by mistake; only my own three files changed (checked by mtime).

**Verification scope (owner-approved cost cut; no full unscoped suite).** All of `packages/engine/test`, `packages/vcs`, `packages/agents`, `packages/templates`, `packages/extensions`, `packages/cli/test/commands/{run,loop,spec}`, `packages/cli/test/{bin-run-plan,bin-run-failures,bin-story-verify,bin-owner-role}.test.ts`, the non-run/loop `packages/cli/test/commands` (failures only in `doctor/rules-delivery`, `upgrade/{backup,run-upgrade}`: other pieces / known load flakes), root `test/{agent-prompts-all-workflows,output-contract-known-gaps,workflows,build-stage-compiles,fm-mobile-workflow,fm-service-workflow,live-smoke,determinism,brief-write-paths-in-claim,run-inputs-compile,write-implies-claim,nine-steps-claims,greenfield-fixture-generated,workspace-floor}.test.ts`; `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm run boundaries`, `eslint`/`prettier` on every file I own (`pnpm lint` also shows other agents' in-flight files). Known flakes seen and passing alone: `crash-resume`, `lane-integration` "concurrency", `elicit-run` crash, `resume.test.ts`, `workspace-floor` (a load timeout and another agent's new test file).

**Files.** `packages/vcs/src/claims.ts`; `packages/engine/src/{dispatch/{outputs,assemble,facades,types,steps,index}.ts,rca/{fix-scan,index}.ts,plan/compile.ts}`; `packages/agents/src/schema/{load,index}.ts`; `packages/cli/src/commands/{implementation-roles.ts,spec.ts,spec/validate-rules.ts,run/{expression-context,run-plan}.ts,doctor/run-doctor.ts}`, `bin.ts` (three `agentsRoot` lines); `packages/core/src/errors/codes.ts` (`RUN-097`); `packages/templates/templates/{workflows/{debug,quick-fix,refactor,migrate,harden,implement-story,build-stage}.workflow.yaml,artifacts/Story.md}`; `specs/{06,09,20}`; the tests above.
